definition_zh: 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时应对；凑合着做；临时搭建
definition_en: to invent or perform something without preparation, using whatever is at hand
core_image: 乐手在台上没有谱子，手指随心情在键上临时走出旋律
scene: 演出开始前才发现要真正表演的曲目没人排练过，乐手们互相看了一眼，决定放开谱子临场发挥。With no rehearsal for the piece, the players glanced at each other and decided to improvise.
sceneCN: 这里 improvise 是「即兴表演、临场发挥」（第 2 个义项：没有准备地现场演出）；句意：这首曲子没排练过，乐手们互相看了一眼，决定即兴演奏。

pos.zh: 即兴表演；临场发挥
即兴创作；临时充作

derivatives.zh: 即兴；即兴作品（improvise 加名词后缀 -ation）
临时凑成的；即兴的（过去分词兼作形容词）
即兴性质的（经意大利语 improviso 加形容词词尾）
即兴演奏者（improvise 加施事后缀 -or，亦作 improviser）

senses.title: To create on the spot
senses.definition: to invent music, lines, or an idea while performing or speaking, without prior preparation
senses.definitionCN: 在表演或说话时当场想出新内容，事先没有准备
senses.example: The trio improvised a whole movement from a single chord.
senses.exampleCN: 三人组从一个和弦出发，即兴演奏了一整个乐章。
senses.why: The Latin root visus means seen, and improvising is doing something without having seen it coming or planned it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 videre/visus 意为「看见」；即兴就是在「事先没有看到」的情况下把事情做出来。

senses.title: To perform without a script
senses.definition: to perform or play without rehearsal, a script, or a planned part
senses.definitionCN: 没有排练、没有稿子、没有既定角色地演出
senses.example: Half the cast was ill, so the others had to improvise.
senses.exampleCN: 一半演员病了，其他人只好临场发挥。
senses.why: Seeing the part in advance is what rehearsal gives, so performing blind is the heart of the sense.
senses.whyCN: 排练的意义正是事先「看见」这一角色；看不见就上，正是这个义项的核心。

senses.title: To handle a problem at once
senses.definition: to deal with an unexpected situation quickly by thinking and acting at once
senses.definitionCN: 遇到突发情况，靠当场思考和行动来处理
senses.example: When the lights went out, the speaker improvised a story in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭了以后，演讲者在黑暗中即兴讲了段故事。
senses.why: Beyond the stage, the unseen event is an emergency, and improvising means answering it right now.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台之外，那个「没预见到的事」就是突发状况，即兴就是立刻回应。

senses.title: To make do with whatever is there
senses.definition: to manage with materials or means that were not designed for the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 用本不是为此准备的材料或手段硬凑出结果
senses.example: We improvised a table from two crates and a plank.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用两个板条箱加一块木板凑成了一张桌子。
senses.why: The same on-the-spot invention, now aimed at things rather than notes.
senses.whyCN: 同样是在现场凭空想出办法，只是对象从音符换成了实物。

senses.title: To put together overnight
senses.definition: to put something together quickly and without proper preparation
senses.definitionCN: 没有充分准备、短时间内临时拼凑出来
senses.example: The team improvised a shelter out of branches before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 团队赶在天黑前用树枝临时搭了个棚子。
senses.why: What is made in a hurry and never seen coming takes the look of an improvised structure.
senses.whyCN: 在匆忙中、毫无预见地做出来的东西，就带有「临时搭建」的样子。

senses.title: To speak without notes
senses.definition: to speak publicly in a talk that was not written out in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先没有写成稿子就公开讲话
senses.example: She improvised a toast that made the whole table laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她即兴致了段祝酒词，逗得满桌人笑起来。
senses.why: Speaking is performance too, and words invented on the spot follow the same unseen path.
senses.whyCN: 说话也是一种表演，当场想出的词句走的是同一条「未预见到」的路。

senses.title: An improvised creation
senses.definition: a work or answer produced spontaneously and then shared
senses.definitionCN: 即兴产生并呈现给他人的作品或答复
senses.example: The afternoon concert was one long improvisation by the two musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 那场下午的音乐会就是两位音乐家的长时间即兴。
senses.why: The verb gives the noun improvisation, which names the made thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词派生出名词 improvisation，用来指那个被做出来的即兴作品。

senses.title: To forge a path
senses.definition: to go forward through uncharted territory by feeling the way as you move
senses.definitionCN: 在未知领域里边摸索边前行
senses.example: The explorers improvised a route when the map ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用尽后，探险者们现找了一条路线。
senses.why: When nothing has been seen ahead, every step is taken as it comes, and the word becomes a way of moving through the unknown.
senses.whyCN: 前方什么都「没看见」时，每一步都走一步算一步，于是这个词也成了穿越未知的姿态。

intro.en: Improvise comes through Italian improviso and French improviser from Latin improvisus, unseen and unforeseen, from in- not plus providere, to foresee.
intro.cn: improvise 经意大利语 improviso 与法语 improviser，源自拉丁语 improvisus（未预见的），由 in-（不）与 providere（预见、预先准备）构成。

items.en: Providere, from pro- ahead and videre to see, means to look ahead and so to provide.
items.cn: providere 由 pro-（向前）与 videre（看）构成，意为「向前看」，进而表示「预备」。

items.en: The adjective improvisus means unforeseen or not provided for.
items.cn: 形容词 improvisus 表示「未预见到的、没有预备的」。

items.en: Italian improviso means sudden or extempore, and improvvisare is the verb for acting on the moment.
items.cn: 意大利语 improviso 意为突然的、即席的，动词 improvvisare 指当场发挥。

items.en: French improviser names the extempore composition of verse and song, and this use reaches English.
items.cn: 法语 improviser 指即席作诗与演唱，这一用法传入英语。

items.en: Improvise is first recorded in English around 1803 for speaking or composing on the spot.
items.cn: improvise 在十九世纪初约 1803 年首次见于英语，指当场讲话或作曲。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to jazz, comedy, resourcing, and everyday second best solutions.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词扩展到爵士乐、喜剧、资源调配与日常应急办法。

note.en: Improvise is the verb of doing without preparation; it looks close to the improvise family and means close to extemporize and ad-lib.
note.cn: improvise 是「没有准备就做」的动词；形式上接近同一词族，意义上接近即兴发挥一类的说法。

entries.definition: the act of improvising
a person who improvises
Latin adjective meaning not foreseeing
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁形容词，意为「不预见的」

entries.definition: not planning ahead for the future
entries.definitionCN: 不未雨绸缪的（与目标词同源于 providere）

entries.definition: to speak or perform without preparation
to say or do something without planning
to create something new
to manage with what is available

normalIntro.en: Improvise is im- plus provide, so to improvise is to act without providing ahead; the unseen, unplanned act.
normalIntro.cn: improvise 是 im- 加 provide：不预先备好就做，就是「没预见到、没安排」地行动。

normal.en: The root is Latin providere, to foresee and prepare, and the negative im- makes the verb mean acting without such preparation.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 providere（预见、预备），否定前缀 im- 让这个动词表示「没有预备就做」。

normal.en: The pair provide and improvise share a root, so think of improvising as not providing in advance.
normal.cn: provide 与 improvise 同根，可以把 improvise 记成「不预先 provide」。

normal.en: The verb has regular forms: improvises, improvised, and improvising.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：improvises、improvised、improvising。

normal.en: Jazz players improvise solos, and comedians improvise scenes on stage.
normal.cn: 爵士乐手即兴独奏，喜剧演员在台上即兴演段子。

normal.en: The noun improvisation keeps the meaning and is widely used for both the act and the work.
normal.cn: 名词 improvisation 保留原义，既指即兴的行为，也指即兴的作品。

abstract.en: Picture a jazz pianist whose hands move before any plan has formed.
abstract.cn: 想象一位爵士钢琴手，手先动起来，计划才刚成形。

abstract.en: Imagine the power going out and the speaker inventing a story in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象突然停电，演讲者在黑暗里现编了一个故事。

abstract.en: Think of a table made of two crates and a plank, solid enough for one dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象两个板条箱加一块木板拼成的桌子，刚好撑过一顿晚饭。

examples.en: The pianist began to improvise around the melody she had just played.
examples.cn: 钢琴家围绕刚弹过的旋律开始即兴演奏。

examples.en: With no script, the actors improvised the final scene.
examples.cn: 没有剧本，演员们即兴演完了最后一幕。

examples.en: We improvised a shelter from branches and a plastic sheet.
examples.cn: 我们用树枝和一块塑料布临时搭了个棚子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「improvised」听来像「硬破歪思」——没有准备也得硬破开一条歪思路往前走，这就是即兴；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 providere（pro- 向前 + videre 看见＝预见、预备）→ 否定形 improvisus（未预见的）→ 意大利语 improviso / improvvisare → 法语 improviser → 英语 improvise，核心义「不预先看见也就照样做出」。

sensesIntro.en: Improvise starts with music invented on the spur of the moment, moves to any performance, problem, or makeshift object made without being seen in advance, and finally names the improvised work itself and the act of moving into the unknown.
sensesIntro.cn: improvise 先指当场想出来的音乐，再扩展到没有预先安排的任何表演、问题应对与临时物件，最后也指即兴作品本身以及走向未知的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a player on stage with no score, letting the fingers find the melody as they go.
core.cn: 核心意象：乐手在台上没有谱子，手指边走边找到旋律。

branches.en: Music invented in the moment is the first and most vivid sense.
branches.cn: 当场想出来的音乐，是第一个也最鲜明的义项。

branches.en: Performing and public speaking without a script both draw on the unseen part.
branches.cn: 无稿表演与即席讲话，都依赖「没预先看见」的部分。

branches.en: An unforeseen emergency and a hurried shelter call for the same reflexes.
branches.cn: 突发状况与匆忙搭建，调用的是同一种现场反应。

branches.en: Making do with available materials is invention aimed at things.
branches.cn: 就地取材、凑合着做，是把创造对准实物。

branches.en: The improvised work and the path through the unknown extend the verb outward.
branches.cn: 即兴作品与穿越未知的路线，把动词向外延伸。

intro.en: Improvise is built on the Latin verb providere, seen through the negating im- and the adjective ending -ise brought in from French and Italian.
intro.cn: improvise 建立在拉丁语动词 providere 之上，经否定前缀 im- 与来自法语的形容词化词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin providere combines pro- ahead with videre to see and means to foresee; improvisus negates it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 providere 由 pro-（在前）与 videre（看）构成，意为预见；improvisus 加以否定。

items.example: The prefix im- negates providere in the source word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 在词源形体中否定 providere。

items.example: The prefix pro- gives the forward look in providere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 在 providere 中表示「向前看」。

items.example: Videre supplies the seeing part of the sense.
items.exampleCN: videre 提供「看见」这层含义。

items.example: The root vid- also appears in evident and vision.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vid- 也见于 evident 与 vision。

items.example: Providere gives both foresee and provide.
items.exampleCN: providere 既给出「预见」也给出「预备」。

items.example: Improvisus is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: improvisus 是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending -ise turns the adjective stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 把形容词词干变成动词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms improvisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 improvisation。

items.meaning: the act or result of improvising
items.example: Improvisation names the act and the work.
items.exampleCN: improvisation 既指行为也指作品。

items.example: The suffix -or forms improvisor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 improvisor。

latinEntries.meaning: to foresee, to take care of

definition_zh: 杂质；不纯；不纯洁；不道德的行为
definition_en: something that makes a substance, a person, or a system no longer pure, or the state of not being pure
core_image: 一池清水里掉进一粒沙，水立刻泛起浑浊
scene: 实验室的试剂瓶里混进了一点灰尘，检测结果因此偏高。A little dust mixed into the reagent bottle, and the reading came out far too high because of that impurity.
sceneCN: 这里 impurity 是「杂质」（第 1 个义项：混入纯净物质中的其他东西）；句意：试剂瓶里混进了一点灰尘，因为这点杂质，检测结果偏高得离谱。

pos.zh: 杂质；不纯；不纯洁；不道德的行为

derivatives.zh: 由 in-（不）+ pure（纯净）构成，义为「不纯的；不洁的」
基础形容词，义为「纯净的；纯粹的」，是 impurity 去掉否定前缀后的核心
pure + -ify（使……化），义为「净化；提纯」
purify + -ation（行为名词后缀），义为「净化；提纯」

senses.title: A substance mixed into another
senses.titleCN: 杂质（物质层面的混入物）
senses.definition: a small amount of an unwanted substance that is mixed with a purer material
senses.definitionCN: 少量不需要的物质混在较纯的物质里面
senses.example: The iron ore contains impurities such as sulphur and phosphorus.
senses.exampleCN: 这块铁矿石含有硫和磷等杂质。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that makes a material impure, so the core image of a grain of sand in clear water becomes a measurable foreign substance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「让材料变得不纯的东西」，于是「清水里的沙粒」这一意象就落实成可测量的外来物质。

senses.title: The state of not being pure
senses.definition: the condition of containing something unwanted, or of being below a standard of purity
senses.definitionCN: 含有不需要之物或纯度达不到标准的状态
senses.example: Tests showed a high level of impurity in the fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 检测显示这批燃料的杂质含量很高。
senses.why: The same abstract noun can name the condition rather than the particles, so the counted grains turn into an uncountable degree of impurity.
senses.whyCN: 同一个抽象名词也可以指状态而不是颗粒本身，于是数得清的沙粒就变成不可数的「不纯程度」。

senses.title: Moral or spiritual impurity
senses.definition: a moral fault or something that is regarded as morally unclean
senses.definitionCN: 道德上的污点，或被看作不洁净的事物
senses.example: Ancient rituals were meant to wash away spiritual impurity.
senses.exampleCN: 古代仪式意在洗去精神上的不洁。
senses.why: Because purity also means moral cleanliness, whatever pollutes a person or a community is called an impurity as well.
senses.whyCN: 因为纯净也指道德上的清白，所以污染个人或社群的东西同样被称作不洁之物。

senses.title: An unwanted element in a system
senses.titleCN: （数据、制度中的）杂质；缺陷成分
senses.definition: an unwanted feature or element that spoils the quality or accuracy of an abstract system
senses.definitionCN: 损害抽象系统质量或准确性的不良成分或因素
senses.example: Gaps in the records are an impurity in the data set.
senses.exampleCN: 记录中的空缺是数据集里的一种杂质。
senses.why: Once purity is a standard, anything that lowers that standard can be called an impurity, even when it is not a physical substance.
senses.whyCN: 一旦纯净成为一种标准，任何拉低这一标准的东西都能叫杂质，即使它并不是实物。

intro.en: Impurity comes from Latin impurus meaning unclean, built from the negative prefix in- and purus meaning clean or pure.
intro.cn: impurity 来自拉丁语 impurus（不洁净的），由否定前缀 in- 与 purus（干净的、纯的）构成。

items.en: Purus means clean or free from mixture, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: purus 意为干净的、不含混合物的，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: Impurus adds the negative prefix and means unclean or impure.
items.cn: impurus 加上否定前缀，意为不洁净的、不纯的。

items.en: The noun impuritas names the quality of being impure.
items.cn: 名词 impuritas 指不纯净的性质。

items.en: The form passes through Old French, where pur and impur describe both metal and morals.
items.cn: 该词形经过古法语，pur 与 impur 既形容金属也形容道德。

items.en: Impurity enters English as a noun for both matter and moral uncleanness.
items.cn: impurity 在十四世纪进入英语，兼指物质杂质与道德不洁。

items.en: Chemistry gives the word its precise sense of measured foreign matter.
items.cn: 化学赋予这个词「可测量的外来物质」这一精确含义。

note.en: Impurity is the noun of not being pure, standing beside impure, purify and pure, and close to contaminant and dirt.
note.cn: impurity 是表示「不纯净」的名词，与 impure、purify、pure 同族，并与 contaminant、dirt 意义相邻。

entries.definition: not pure, mixed with something else
entries.definitionCN: 不纯的；混有其他东西的

entries.definition: to remove impurities from something
clean and free from anything unwanted
a harmful substance that spoils another
entries.definitionCN: 污染另一物质的污染物

entries.definition: unwanted matter such as dust or soil
a substance that makes air or water dirty
entries.definitionCN: 污染空气或水源的物质

normalIntro.en: Impurity is the negative partner of purity: one unwanted grain standing in a clean pool.
normalIntro.cn: impurity 是 purity 的否定搭档：一粒多余的东西立在清池里。

normal.en: Impurity splits into im- (not) plus purity, so it means not pure.
normal.cn: impurity 可拆成 im-（不）加 purity，意思就是「不纯」。

normal.en: Impure is the matching adjective, so impurity is its noun.
normal.cn: impure 是对应形容词，impurity 就是它的名词。

normal.en: To remove impurities is the standard collocation in chemistry.
normal.cn: remove impurities 是化学语境的标准搭配。

normal.en: Trace impurities means tiny amounts of unwanted matter.
normal.cn: trace impurities 指极微量的多余物质。

normal.en: Compare purity: same family, opposite value of im-.
normal.cn: 对比 purity：同属一个词族，差别只在于 im- 表示否定。

abstract.en: Picture a clear glass of water clouding when one grain of sand falls in.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯清水，一粒沙落进去就成了浑浊。

abstract.en: Imagine a white shirt with a single dark smudge that cannot be washed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白衬衫上有一块洗不掉的深色污点。

abstract.en: Think of a clean record suddenly ruined by one bad page.
abstract.cn: 想象一份干净的档案被一页坏纸毁掉。

examples.en: The filter removes impurities from the drinking water.
examples.cn: 过滤器去除饮用水中的杂质。

examples.en: High levels of impurities can weaken the steel.
examples.cn: 杂质含量过高会削弱钢材强度。

examples.en: Chemists measure the purity of a sample by its impurities.
examples.cn: 化学家通过杂质含量来衡量样本的纯度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬泼油」——硬把油泼进清水，水就浑了，成了杂质；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ purus（纯净）→ impurus（不洁的）→ impuritas（不净）→ 古法语 → 英语 impurity，核心义「混进来的不纯之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Impurity first names a foreign substance mixed into a material, then the state of lacking purity, and finally moral or abstract defects.
sensesIntro.cn: impurity 先指混入材料中的外来物质，再指缺乏纯净的状态，最后引申到道德或抽象系统里的缺陷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain of sand sinking into a pool of clear water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒沙沉进一池清水。

branches.en: The grain itself is the concrete sense of a foreign substance.
branches.cn: 那粒沙本身就是「外来物质」这一具体义项。

branches.en: Small particles together give the uncountable sense of low purity.
branches.cn: 许多小颗粒合起来，就得到「纯度不足」这一不可数义项。

branches.en: Moral uncleanness is the metaphorical sense.
branches.cn: 道德上的不洁是隐喻义项。

branches.en: A chemical impurity and a data flaw are both unwanted elements.
branches.cn: 化学杂质与数据缺陷都是多余的不良成分。

branches.en: Both describe a lowering of a standard, physical or moral.
branches.cn: 两者都描述某种标准的降低，一为物质、一为道德。

intro.en: Impurity is the negative branch of the Latin purus family, with pure, purify, impure and purification around it.
intro.cn: impurity 是拉丁语 purus 词族的否定分支，周围有 pure、purify、impure 与 purification。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and purus means clean or free from mixture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，purus 表示「干净的、不含混合物的」。

items.example: In- before p often becomes im-, as in impure.
items.exampleCN: in- 在 p 前常变为 im-，如 impure。

items.example: Purus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: purus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Impurus joins the negative prefix to purus.
items.exampleCN: impurus 把否定前缀加到 purus 上。

items.meaningCN: 表性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms abstract nouns like purity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 purity 这类抽象名词。

items.example: Purity is the positive partner of impurity.
items.exampleCN: purity 是 impurity 的反义搭档。

items.example: Impure describes a mixture that is not clean.
items.exampleCN: impure 描述不干净的混合物。

items.example: Purify removes unwanted matter.
items.exampleCN: purify 指去除多余物质。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms purify from pure.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 由 pure 构成 purify。

definition_zh: 不准确的；不精确的；有错误的
definition_en: not correct or exact, especially because of a small error or a failure to measure carefully
core_image: 一把刻度歪了的尺子，量出来的长度总是差一截
scene: 天气预报说周末晴朗，结果下了一整天大雨。The forecast said the weekend would be sunny, but it rained all day because the prediction was so inaccurate.
sceneCN: 这里 inaccurate 是「不准确的」（第 1 个义项：得出或给出的结果与事实不符）；句意：预报说周末晴朗，却下了一整天大雨，因为这个预测太不准确了。

pos.zh: 不准确的；不精确的；有错误的

collocations.zh: 失真的图景；不准确的印象

derivatives.zh: inaccurate 去掉 -e 加 -cy，义为「不准确；不准确之处」
基础形容词，义为「准确的；精确的」，是 inaccurate 去掉否定前缀后的核心
inaccurate + -ly，义为「不准确地；不精确地」
accurate 的名词形式，义为「准确性；精确度」，与 inaccuracy 构成正反对照

senses.title: Not matching the facts
senses.definition: giving information that is wrong or only partly true
senses.definitionCN: 提供的信息是错误的或只有一部分属实
senses.example: The article contains several inaccurate statements about the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章里有几处关于战争的陈述与事实不符。
senses.why: Latin in- negates accurate, so whatever does not hit the mark exactly is described as inaccurate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 否定 accurate，于是凡是没有精确命中目标的事物都被说成不准确。

senses.title: Not exact in measurement
senses.definition: not exact or precise, especially in a measurement or a calculation
senses.definitionCN: 不精确，尤指测量或计算上的偏差
senses.example: Inaccurate scales can cost a shop a lot of money.
senses.exampleCN: 不准的秤可能让商店损失很多钱。
senses.why: The core image is a crooked ruler, so the word naturally describes anything that measures or counts with a margin of error.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一把歪尺子，因此这个词天然用来形容任何带误差的测量或计数。

senses.title: Not true to life
senses.definition: not giving a fair or faithful picture of something
senses.definitionCN: 没有公正或忠实地呈现某事物的样子
senses.example: The film gives an inaccurate picture of life in the countryside.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片对乡村生活的呈现是失真的。
senses.why: If a description does not reproduce the original faithfully, it misses the mark just as a bad measurement does.
senses.whyCN: 如果描述没有忠实还原原貌，它就和糟糕的测量一样偏离了目标。

senses.title: Careless in aim or action
senses.definition: not hitting the intended target because of careless aim or movement
senses.definitionCN: 因瞄准或动作不慎而没有击中目标
senses.example: Inaccurate passing cost the team the match.
senses.exampleCN: 不准的传球让球队输掉了比赛。
senses.why: The same negative prefix can attach to a physical act, so a pass or a shot that fails to reach its target is also called inaccurate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个否定前缀也能修饰身体动作，因此没能到达目标的传球或射门同样叫不准确。

intro.en: Inaccurate joins the negative prefix in- to accurate, which comes from Latin accuratus, meaning carefully done.
intro.cn: inaccurate 由否定前缀 in- 加 accurate 构成，而 accurate 来自拉丁语 accuratus（精心完成的）。

items.en: Cura means care or attention, the root that later yields both cure and accuracy.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、用心，是后来 cure 与 accuracy 共同的词根。

items.en: Accuratus means done with care, from ad- plus curare, to take care of.
items.cn: accuratus 意为用心做成，由 ad- 加 curare（照料）构成。

items.en: Scientific use gives accuratus the sense of exact and precise.
items.cn: 科学用法让 accuratus 带上了精确、准确的含义。

items.en: Accurate enters English as exact, and the negative in- form follows in the same century.
items.cn: accurate 在十七世纪以「精确的」进入英语，带否定前缀 in- 的形式也在同一世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English uses inaccurate for reports, measurements, and data.
items.cn: 现代英语把 inaccurate 用于报道、测量与数据。

note.en: Inaccurate is the negative of accurate, standing beside inaccuracy, inaccurate usage and exact, and close to inexact and wrong.
note.cn: inaccurate 是 accurate 的否定形式，与 inaccuracy、inaccurately 同族，并与 inexact、wrong 意义相邻。

entries.definition: correct and exact in every detail
a mistake or lack of exactness
in a way that is not exact or correct
not completely precise
entries.definitionCN: 不精确的；不完全准确的

entries.definition: not correct in fact
giving a false idea or impression
entries.definitionCN: 误导的；使人产生错误印象的

normalIntro.en: Inaccurate is accurate with a negative in- in front: the ruler is there, but it misses the mark.
normalIntro.cn: inaccurate 是在 accurate 前加上否定的 in-：尺子还在，只是偏离了刻度。

normal.en: In- means not and accurate means exact, so inaccurate means not exact.
normal.cn: in- 表示「不」，accurate 表示「精确」，所以 inaccurate 就是「不精确」。

normal.en: The noun is inaccuracy, and the adverb is inaccurately.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 inaccuracy，副词形式是 inaccurately。

normal.en: Inaccurate information is a common phrase in news and research.
normal.cn: inaccurate information 是新闻与研究中的常见搭配。

normal.en: Inaccurate measurements ruin experiments more often than bad theory.
normal.cn: 毁掉实验的往往是测量不准，而不是理论错误。

normal.en: Compare wrong: wrong is totally false, inaccurate is slightly or partly off.
normal.cn: 对比 wrong：wrong 是完全错误，inaccurate 是略有或部分偏差。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one street is drawn one block too far north.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，把某条街画偏了一个街区。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock that is always three minutes slow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只总是慢三分钟的钟。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph printed slightly blurred at the edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一张照片冲印出来边缘略有模糊。

examples.en: The survey was criticized for giving an inaccurate picture of the town.
examples.cn: 这项调查因对小城情况呈现失真而受到批评。

examples.en: Old maps are often inaccurate about distance.
examples.cn: 旧地图在距离上往往不准确。

examples.en: Data from unreliable sources can be dangerously inaccurate.
examples.cn: 来自不可靠来源的数据可能错得很危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印，客，录的」——印出来的客户记录常出错，数据不准确；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ ad-（向）+ curare（用心照料）→ accuratus（精心完成的）→ accurate（精确的）→ 加否定前缀 → inaccurate，核心义「没对准目标」。

sensesIntro.en: Inaccurate starts from a statement or measurement that misses the facts, then extends to descriptions that distort reality and actions that fail to hit a target.
sensesIntro.cn: inaccurate 从「与事实不符的陈述或测量」出发，再扩展到失真的描述与没能命中目标的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler whose marks are off, so every length comes out wrong.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻度偏了的尺子，量出的长度总是错的。

branches.en: Statements that do not match the facts are the most common sense.
branches.cn: 与事实不符的陈述是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Measurements and numbers give the technical sense.
branches.cn: 测量与数字构成技术义项。

branches.en: Distorted descriptions and images form the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 失真的描述与画面构成比喻义项。

branches.en: A crooked ruler and an off-target pass both miss the mark.
branches.cn: 歪尺子与偏离目标的传球都同样没对准。

branches.en: Both concern how faithfully reality is represented in words or pictures.
branches.cn: 两者都关乎文字或图像对现实的还原程度。

intro.en: Inaccurate is built from the negative prefix in- and accurate, which belongs to the Latin cura family.
intro.cn: inaccurate 由否定前缀 in- 与 accurate 构成，而 accurate 属于拉丁语 cura 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and accuratus means done carefully, from cura, care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，accuratus 意为精心完成的，源于 cura（关心、用心）。

items.example: In- turns accurate into inaccurate.
items.exampleCN: in- 把 accurate 变成 inaccurate。

items.example: Cura is the root of accurate.
items.exampleCN: cura 是 accurate 的词根。

items.example: Accuratus is the source of accurate.
items.exampleCN: accuratus 是 accurate 的来源。

items.example: Accurate is the positive base of inaccurate.
items.exampleCN: accurate 是 inaccurate 的肯定基础。

items.meaningCN: 具有某性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate appears in accurate.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀 -ate 出现在 accurate 里。

items.meaningCN: 表状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -cy forms inaccuracy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 inaccuracy。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inaccurately.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 inaccurately。

items.example: Accuracy is the positive noun.
items.exampleCN: accuracy 是对应的肯定名词。

definition_zh: 不活跃的；不活动的；停用的；闲置的
definition_en: not doing anything, not working, or not taking part in activity
core_image: 一台落了灰的机器，开关关着，齿轮一动不动
scene: 银行发现这张卡半年没有任何交易，就把账户转成了休眠账户。The bank noticed there had been no payments for half a year, so it marked the account as inactive.
sceneCN: 这里 inactive 是「不活跃的；闲置的」（第 2 个义项：账户、设备等处于停用或休眠状态）；句意：银行发现这张卡半年没有任何交易，就把账户标记为不活跃。

pos.zh: 不活跃的；不活动的；停用的；闲置的

derivatives.zh: inactive 去掉 -e 加 -ity，义为「不活动；不活跃」
基础形容词，义为「活跃的；积极的」，是 inactive 去掉否定前缀后的核心
inactive + -ly，义为「不活跃地」
in- + activate，义为「使失去活性；使停用」

senses.title: Not doing physical activity
senses.definition: not moving much or not doing physical exercise
senses.definitionCN: 很少活动或缺乏体育锻炼
senses.example: People who are inactive have a higher risk of heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 不活动的人患心脏病的风险更高。
senses.why: Latin in- negates active, so a person who does not perform an act is simply not active.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 否定 active，因此没有从事活动的人就是「不活跃的」。

senses.title: Not in use or shut down
senses.definition: not being used, operated, or working at present
senses.definitionCN: 当前没有被使用、运行或起作用
senses.example: The alarm stays inactive until the door is opened.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门被打开之前，警报器一直处于关闭状态。
senses.why: A machine that is switched off keeps its shape but does nothing, so use gives the word a second, thing-centred sense.
senses.whyCN: 关掉的机器外形还在，却什么也不做，于是这个词在器物上长出了第二个义项。

senses.title: Not taking part
senses.definition: not joining in the work or life of a group, club, or community
senses.definitionCN: 不参与团体、俱乐部或社区的工作与生活
senses.example: She has been an inactive member of the club for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年来她一直是这个俱乐部里不活跃的会员。
senses.why: When the subject is a person inside a group, being inactive means failing to take part, not simply resting.
senses.whyCN: 当主语是团体里的人时，不活跃意味着没有参与，而不只是休息。

senses.title: Chemically or biologically inactive
senses.definition: having no chemical or biological effect when applied
senses.definitionCN: 施用后没有化学或生物效应
senses.example: Some pills contain inactive ingredients such as sugar and colouring.
senses.exampleCN: 有些药片含有糖和色素等非活性成分。
senses.why: Laboratory use narrows the general negative to substances that have no effect, contrasting them with active compounds.
senses.whyCN: 实验用语把一般性的否定收窄到「没有效应的物质」，与活性成分相对。

senses.title: Dormant in a natural system
senses.definition: existing in a quiet, resting condition and ready to start again
senses.definitionCN: 处于安静休止的状态，并可能重新开始
senses.example: The volcano has been inactive for more than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座火山已经休眠了一个多世纪。
senses.why: In nature, not acting does not mean dead; the system rests, so the word extends to sleeping volcanoes and dormant seeds.
senses.whyCN: 在自然界里，不活动不等于死去，而是休止待发，于是这个词扩展到休眠的火山与种子。

intro.en: Inactive is the negative prefix in- joined to active, which comes from Latin actus, a doing or a drive.
intro.cn: inactive 是否定前缀 in- 加 active，而 active 来自拉丁语 actus（行动、驱动）。

items.en: The verb agere means to do or to drive, and gives the participle actus, a doing.
items.cn: 动词 agere 意为做、驱动，其分词 actus 意为行动。

items.en: Activus means busy or engaged in doing, formed from actus with the adjective suffix.
items.cn: activus 意为繁忙的、忙于做事的，由 actus 加形容词后缀构成。

items.en: The adjective enters French as actif, carrying the sense of doing rather than merely being.
items.cn: 该形容词以 actif 进入法语，带出「动手去做」而不只是「存在着」的含义。

items.en: Active arrives in English, and the negated form inactive follows in the next century.
items.cn: active 在十四世纪进入英语，带否定前缀的 inactive 在随后一个世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English applies inactive to people, devices, accounts, and compounds.
items.cn: 现代英语把 inactive 用于人、设备、账户与化合物。

note.en: Inactive is the negative of active, standing beside inactivity and inactivate, and close to dormant, idle and passive.
note.cn: inactive 是 active 的否定形式，与 inactivity、inactivate 同族，并与 dormant、idle、passive 意义相邻。

entries.definition: busy doing things or working
the state of not doing anything
to make something no longer work
sleeping or not active yet, but able to become active
entries.definitionCN: 休眠的；暂停但可恢复的

entries.definition: not working or not being used
accepting what happens without taking action

normalIntro.en: Inactive is active with a negative in- in front: the machine is still there, but nothing moves.
normalIntro.cn: inactive 是在 active 前加上否定的 in-：机器还在，但什么也不动。

normal.en: In- means not and active means working, so inactive means not working.
normal.cn: in- 表示「不」，active 表示「在工作」，所以 inactive 就是「不工作」。

normal.en: Active comes from agere, to do, so inactive is literally not doing.
normal.cn: active 源于 agere（去做），所以 inactive 字面就是「不做」。

normal.en: The noun is inactivity and the verb is inactivate.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 inactivity，动词形式是 inactivate。

normal.en: An inactive account is one that has not been used for a long time.
normal.cn: inactive account 指很久没有使用过的账户。

normal.en: Compare dormancy: plants and volcanoes are said to be dormant, machines are said to be inactive.
normal.cn: 对比休眠：植物与火山多用 dormant，机器多用 inactive。

abstract.en: Picture a bicycle leaning against a wall for years, its tyres flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆靠在墙边多年的自行车，轮胎都瘪了。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone screen that stays dark until you touch it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块不碰就不亮的手机屏。

abstract.en: Think of a membership card that expires because nobody uses it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张因为无人使用而过期的会员卡。

examples.en: Many older people become inactive after they retire.
examples.cn: 许多老年人在退休后变得不活动。

examples.en: The software marks accounts inactive after six months without a login.
examples.cn: 该软件会在半年没有登录后把账户标记为不活跃。

examples.en: Scientists studied the chemistry of inactive viruses.
examples.cn: 科学家研究了失活病毒的化学性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬，爱克踢我」——机器硬是爱踢我，说明它不听话、不干活，处于不活跃状态；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 agere（去做、驱动）→ actus（行动）→ activus（忙碌做事的）→ 英语 active → 加否定前缀 in- → inactive，核心义「开关关着」。

sensesIntro.en: Inactive begins with people who do not move, extends to devices and accounts that are shut down, then to groups that take no part, and finally to compounds and natural systems that rest.
sensesIntro.cn: inactive 先从「不动的人」说起，扩展到「停用的设备与账户」，再到「不参与的团体」，最后落到「非活性的成分」与「休眠的自然系统」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dusty machine with its switch turned off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台落灰的机器，开关关着。

branches.en: A person who does not move enough is the basic human sense.
branches.cn: 活动不足的人是基础的人身义项。

branches.en: Devices and accounts that are switched off form the object sense.
branches.cn: 关停的设备与账户构成器物义项。

branches.en: Not taking part in a group is the social sense.
branches.cn: 不参与团体是社交义项。

branches.en: An inactive person and an inactive member both fail to act.
branches.cn: 不活动的人与不活跃的会员都没有行动。

branches.en: Non-active compounds and dormant systems are resting, not dead.
branches.cn: 非活性成分与休眠系统是休止，而非消亡。

intro.en: Inactive is the negative branch of the Latin agere family, with act, active, action and activity around it.
intro.cn: inactive 是拉丁语 agere 词族的否定分支，周围有 act、active、action 与 activity。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and activus means busy doing, from actus, a doing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，activus 意为忙于做事的，源于 actus（行动）。

items.example: In- turns active into inactive.
items.exampleCN: in- 把 active 变成 inactive。

items.example: Agere is the deepest root of active.
items.exampleCN: agere 是 active 的最深词根。

items.example: Actus gives English act.
items.exampleCN: actus 构成英语的 act。

items.example: Activus is the direct source of active.
items.exampleCN: activus 是 active 的直接来源。

items.meaning: tending to or having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 表倾向或性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms active.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 active。

items.example: Active is the positive base of inactive.
items.exampleCN: active 是 inactive 的肯定基础。

items.meaningCN: 表状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms inactivity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 inactivity。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms inactivate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 inactivate。

definition_zh: 不充分的；不足的；不合格的；不胜任的
definition_en: not enough in amount or quality, or not good enough for a purpose or position
core_image: 一只水杯只剩半杯水，够不着杯口的刻度线
scene: 宿舍热水供应不足，洗澡常常只能顶着一身冷水。The hostel has inadequate hot water, so residents often shower cold.
sceneCN: 这里 inadequate 是「不充分、不够量」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度达不到需要）；句意：宿舍热水供应不足，住客常常只能洗冷水澡。

pos.zh: 不充分的；不足的；不合格的；不胜任的

collocations.zh: 感到力不从心；感到自己不够好

derivatives.zh: 由 -acy 后缀把形容词变名词，义为「不充分；不胜任」
由 -ly 后缀构成副词，义为「不充分地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的反义原形，义为「足够的；胜任的」

senses.title: Not enough in amount
senses.definition: not enough for what is needed in size, quantity, or extent
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或程度上达不到需要
senses.example: The lighting in the room was inadequate for reading.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的灯光不足以看书。
senses.why: The root Latin adaequare means to make equal, so in- plus equal marks a supply that never levels up to the demand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 adaequare 意为「使相等」，in- 加「相等」就表示供给始终配不上需求。

senses.title: Not good enough in quality
senses.definition: not of a high enough standard to do a job or pass a test
senses.definitionCN: 标准不够高，无法完成工作或通过检验
senses.example: The court ruled that the evidence was inadequate.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭裁定证据不够充分。
senses.why: From quantity the word easily shifts to quality: the amount is there, but the standard still falls short of the mark.
senses.whyCN: 从数量自然过渡到质量：量虽然有了，标准却依然够不到。

senses.title: Not able to cope
senses.definition: unable to deal with a task, role, or situation because of a lack of ability or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 因能力或信心不足而无法应对任务、角色或处境
senses.example: He felt inadequate in front of so many experts.
senses.exampleCN: 在那么多专家面前，他感到自己力不从心。
senses.why: The same image applies to people: a person whose abilities do not measure up to the job is judged inadequate.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象也用于人：能力与任务不相称的人就被判为不胜任。

intro.en: Inadequate joins the negative prefix in- to adequate, which comes from Latin adaequare, to make equal to.
intro.cn: inadequate 由否定前缀 in- 加 adequate 构成，adequate 来自拉丁语 adaequare（使相等）。

items.en: Adaequare means to make equal to or to level up to a standard.
items.cn: adaequare 意为使之相等、使达到某个标准。

items.en: Adequatus, the past participle, means made equal.
items.cn: 过去分词 adaequatus 意为「被使之相等的」。

items.en: Adequate keeps the sense of matching what is required.
items.cn: adequate 保留「与所需相称」的意思。

items.en: English borrows adequate to mean equal to the purpose.
items.cn: 英语借入 adequate，意为与目的相称。

items.en: The negative in- plus adequate gives inadequate, meaning not sufficient.
items.cn: 加否定前缀 in- 后的 inadequate 表示不充分。

items.en: Modern English extends inadequate to people, evidence, housing, and services.
items.cn: 现代英语把 inadequate 扩展到人、证据、住房与服务。

note.en: Inadequate belongs to the family of adequate, inadequacy, and the wider group of shortfall words.
note.cn: inadequate 与 adequate、inadequacy 同属一个词族，并与一整组表示「不足」的词相邻。

entries.definition: enough or good enough for the purpose
the state of not being enough
in a way that is not sufficient
not enough in amount
lacking something necessary
of low quality

normalIntro.en: Inadequate is an equation that never balances: what you have cannot equal what you need.
normalIntro.cn: inadequate 是一道配不平的等式：手头的东西怎么也对不上需要的量。

normal.en: Inadequate for a task means simply not enough for it.
normal.cn: inadequate for 某事，就是为这件事不够用。

normal.en: Feel inadequate is a common phrase for feeling not good enough.
normal.cn: feel inadequate 是常用说法，指觉得自己不够好。

normal.en: Inadequate supply and inadequate training both describe shortfalls.
normal.cn: inadequate supply 与 inadequate training 都描述不足。

normal.en: Compare insufficient: the two are close, but inadequate often adds a note of quality.
normal.cn: 对比 insufficient：两者接近，但 inadequate 常多一层「质量」意味。

normal.en: The noun inadequacy names the shortfall itself.
normal.cn: 名词 inadequacy 指不足本身。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with too few weights on one pan.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，一端放的砝码太少。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge too short to reach the far bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一座短了几步、够不到对岸的桥。

abstract.en: Imagine stepping onto a stage and feeling smaller than the role.
abstract.cn: 想象走上舞台，觉得自己撑不起那个角色。

examples.en: The team lost because their training was inadequate.
examples.cn: 球队输了，因为训练不够充分。

examples.en: Many villages still have inadequate access to clean water.
examples.cn: 许多村庄获得清洁水的条件仍然不足。

examples.en: She felt inadequate when asked to lead the meeting.
examples.cn: 被要求主持会议时，她感到自己力不从心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「应得亏」——该给的量没给足，就是不足；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ adaequare（使相等）→ adequatus（相称的）→ 英语 adequate → 加否定前缀 in- 得 inadequate，核心义「配不上所需的标准」。

sensesIntro.en: Inadequate starts from not enough in amount, moves to not good enough in quality, and finally describes a person who cannot cope.
sensesIntro.cn: inadequate 从「数量不足」出发，转到「质量不达标」，最后指向「人无法应对」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale that never balances against the need.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台怎么也称不平的天平。

branches.en: Short supply in amount is the first sense.
branches.cn: 数量上的不足是第一个义项。

branches.en: Shortfall in quality is the second sense.
branches.cn: 质量上的不达标是第二个义项。

branches.en: A person who cannot cope is the third sense.
branches.cn: 无法应对的人属于第三个义项。

branches.en: Supplies and standards are both measured against a requirement.
branches.cn: 供给与标准都要对照某个要求来衡量。

branches.en: Having too little resources and having too little ability share one image.
branches.cn: 资源太少与能力太小共用同一个意象。

intro.en: Inadequate is built from the negative prefix in- and adequate, which traces to Latin adaequare.
intro.cn: inadequate 由否定前缀 in- 与 adequate 构成，adequate 可追溯到拉丁语 adaequare。

latinIntro.en: Latin adaequare, to make equal, gives adaequatus and then English adequate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adaequare 意为使相等，由此有 adaequatus，再进入英语成为 adequate。

items.example: Before consonants the prefix in- forms inadequate, incomplete, and insecure.
items.exampleCN: 在辅音前，前缀 in- 构成 inadequate、incomplete 与 insecure。

items.example: The prefix ad- opens adaequare.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 出现在 adaequare 的词首。

items.example: Aequus gives the equal image behind adequate.
items.exampleCN: aequus 为 adequate 提供相等的意象。

items.example: Adaequare means to level something up to a standard.
items.exampleCN: adaequare 意为把某物配到某个标准。

items.example: Adequate is the basis of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: adequate 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Inadequate negates adequate.
items.exampleCN: inadequate 是否定 adequate 的形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -acy forms inadequacy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -acy 构成 inadequacy。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inadequately.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 inadequately。

definition_zh: 不可剥夺的；不可让渡的；天生的
definition_en: impossible to take away, give up, or transfer to another person
core_image: 一枚刻进掌心纹路里的印章，谁也擦不掉
scene: 宣言里写着，生命与自由的权利人人生而有之，任何政府也夺不走。The declaration says that the right to life and liberty is inalienable, and no government can take it away.
sceneCN: 这里 inalienable 是「不可剥夺的」（第 1 个义项：不能被夺走或转让的权利）；句意：宣言称生命与自由的权利不可剥夺，任何政府都夺不走。

pos.zh: 不可剥夺的；不可让渡的；天生的

derivatives.zh: 由 -ity 后缀把形容词变名词，义为「不可剥夺性」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的反义原形，义为「可转让的」
同根的动词，义为「转让；使疏远」

senses.title: That cannot be taken away
senses.definition: describing a right or freedom that no one, including the state, may remove
senses.definitionCN: 指任何力量包括国家都不能夺走的权利或自由
senses.example: Freedom of speech is seen as an inalienable right.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由被视为一项不可剥夺的权利。
senses.why: Latin alienare means to transfer to another owner, so in- plus alienare means something that can never be handed over or taken.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alienare 意为转让给别人，in- 加 alienare 就表示永远不能转手或被拿走的东西。

senses.title: That cannot be given up or transferred
senses.titleCN: 不可让渡的；不可转让的
senses.definition: describing property or a legal status that its holder cannot sell, give, or transfer
senses.definitionCN: 指持有人不能出售、赠予或转让的财产或法律地位
senses.example: In some systems a family plot is inalienable and cannot be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些制度下，家族用地不可让渡，不能出售。
senses.why: In law the word keeps the narrowest part of the root meaning: transfer is simply ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 法律上这个词保留了词根最窄的一层意思：转让被彻底排除。

senses.title: So close it cannot be separated
senses.titleCN: 无法分割的；与生俱来的
senses.definition: used of a trait or part of something that belongs to it so deeply that it cannot be cut off
senses.definitionCN: 指某属性或部分与事物结合得极深，无法割裂
senses.example: The river is an inalienable part of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河是小镇无法分割的一部分。
senses.why: From what cannot be taken away comes a broader image: something so attached that it cannot be parted from its owner.
senses.whyCN: 从「拿不走」引申为更广的画面：附着得极紧，割不开也分不了。

intro.en: Inalienable combines the negative prefix in- with alienable, from Latin alienare, to transfer something to another owner.
intro.cn: inalienable 由否定前缀 in- 与 alienable 组合而成，alienable 来自拉丁语 alienare（使归属他人）。

items.en: Alienus means belonging to another and also strange.
items.cn: alienus 意为属于他人的，也有「陌生的」之意。

items.en: Alienare means to make over to another owner.
items.cn: alienare 意为转让给他人。

items.en: Alius, meaning other, stands behind alienus as a related form.
items.cn: 意为「另一个」的 alius 是 alienus 的相关形式。

items.en: Lawyers use inalienable for property that the owner cannot transfer.
items.cn: 十七世纪律师用 inalienable 指业主不能转让的财产。

items.en: Political writers apply the word to natural rights that no ruler may remove.
items.cn: 十八世纪政治写作者用它指任何统治者都不能剥夺的天赋人权。

items.en: The word now also describes features so close that they cannot be separated.
items.cn: 现代英语中它也可指无法分割的组成部分。

note.en: Inalienable sits with alien, alienate, and alienable at its root, and near rights words such as inherent and indivisible.
note.cn: inalienable 在词根上与 alien、alienate、alienable 相邻，在意义与 inherent、indivisible 这类权利词相近。

entries.definition: belonging to another country or being strange
to transfer property or to make someone unfriendly
able to be transferred to another owner
existing as a natural and permanent part
not able to be divided or separated
not able to be attacked or taken away
entries.definitionCN: 无法攻破的；无可动摇的

normalIntro.en: Inalienable says that the thing was never yours to hand to someone else, so it can never be taken either.
normalIntro.cn: inalienable 的意思是：这东西本来就不能交给别人，因此也没人能把它拿走。

normal.en: Inalienable rights is the most common collocation of the word.
normal.cn: 不可剥夺的权利是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: An inalienable part of something cannot be cut off from it.
normal.cn: 某事物不可分割的一部分就是切不掉的部分。

normal.en: The word pairs with legal terms such as ownership and possession.
normal.cn: 这个词常与所有权、占有这类法律词汇搭配。

normal.en: Compare alienable: the negative in- is doing all the work.
normal.cn: 对比 alienable：关键在于否定的 in-。

normal.en: The shared root with alien reminds you of belonging to another.
normal.cn: 与 alien 同根，提醒你它的本义是归属他人。

abstract.en: Picture a seal pressed so deep into skin that no cloth can rub it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章压进皮肤深处，怎么擦都擦不掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a land deed nailed to the door so it cannot be sold.
abstract.cn: 想象一份地契钉在门上，谁也卖不出去。

abstract.en: Think of a tree whose roots run under the whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树的根系伸到整个镇子底下，移不走。

examples.en: The charter lists life and liberty as inalienable rights.
examples.cn: 宪章把生命与自由列为不可剥夺的权利。

examples.en: Under the old rules, this land was inalienable and could not be sold.
examples.cn: 按旧规，这块土地不可让渡，不能出售。

examples.en: Sea and stone are an inalienable part of the island identity.
examples.cn: 大海与石头是这座岛屿身份中无法分割的部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「姻连里」——姻亲连理一样割不断的关系，就是不可剥夺；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ alienare（使归属他人，源于 alienus 属于他人的）+ -able（能……的）→ inalienable，核心义「不能被转手，也就夺不走」。

sensesIntro.en: Inalienable begins with rights that no power may remove, narrows to property that cannot be sold, and widens again to anything deeply attached.
sensesIntro.cn: inalienable 先指任何权力都夺不走的权利，再窄化为不能出售的财产，最后又扩展为一切割不开的部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal cut into the hand that no one can rub away.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻进手心的印记，谁也擦不掉。

branches.en: Rights that cannot be removed form the political sense.
branches.cn: 夺不走的权利构成政治义项。

branches.en: Property that cannot be transferred is the legal sense.
branches.cn: 不能转让的财产是法律义项。

branches.en: Being unable to be parted is the broad sense.
branches.cn: 割不开、分不了是引申义项。

branches.en: Both rights and land are things the holder cannot trade away.
branches.cn: 权利与土地都是持有人无法交换出去的东西。

branches.en: A right born with a person feels as close as a part of the body.
branches.cn: 与生俱来的权利贴近得像身体的一部分。

intro.en: Inalienable is in- plus alienable, built on the Latin root alienus, belonging to another.
intro.cn: inalienable 是 in- 加 alienable，基底是拉丁词根 alienus（属于他人的）。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius and alienus mean other, and alienare means to make over to another owner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 与 alienus 意为「另外的、他人的」，alienare 意为转让他人。

items.example: The prefix in- negates alienable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定 alienable。

items.example: Alius is the old other behind alienus.
items.exampleCN: alius 是 alienus 背后更古老的「另外」。

items.example: Alienus carries both ownership and strangeness.
items.exampleCN: alienus 同时带有归属与陌生两层意思。

items.example: Alienare is the act of handing something over.
items.exampleCN: alienare 就是把手头的东西交出去。

items.example: The suffix -able makes alienable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 alienable。

items.example: Alienable is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: alienable 是基础形容词。

items.example: Inalienable negates the transfer.
items.exampleCN: inalienable 否定转让。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms inalienability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 inalienability。

items.example: Alien keeps the other sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: alien 保留了词根「他者」的含义。

definition_zh: 不合适的；不合时宜的；不恰当的；不适龄的
definition_en: not suitable or right for a particular situation, person, or purpose
core_image: 盛夏婚礼上有人穿了一件厚羽绒服
scene: 答辩会场上有人对着导师大吼大叫，这种做法显然很不合时宜。Shouting at the examiner during the defence was clearly inappropriate.
sceneCN: 这里 inappropriate 是「不合时宜、不恰当」（第 1 个义项：不适合当前场合或情境）；句意：答辩时冲考官大吼，显然很不合时宜。

pos.zh: 不合适的；不合时宜的；不恰当的；不适龄的

derivatives.zh: 由 -ly 后缀构成副词，义为「不恰当地」
由 -ness 后缀构成名词，义为「不恰当」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的反义原形，义为「合适的」

senses.title: Not suitable for the situation
senses.titleCN: 不合时宜的；不适合场合的
senses.definition: not right or suitable for a particular occasion, place, or moment
senses.definitionCN: 对某个场合、地点或时刻来说不对、不合适
senses.example: Jokes about the accident were inappropriate at the memorial.
senses.exampleCN: 在追悼会上开那场事故的玩笑很不合时宜。
senses.why: Latin proprius means ones own, and the verb appropriare means to make something fit its purpose, so in- marks whatever does not fit the setting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，动词 appropriare 意为使之合用，in- 就标出一切与场合对不上的东西。

senses.title: Not good enough for the purpose
senses.titleCN: 不恰当的；方法不得当的
senses.definition: not the right choice of method or words for the task in hand
senses.definitionCN: 对所办的事情来说，选的方法或措辞不对
senses.example: The teacher used an inappropriate method for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对初学者用了不恰当的方法。
senses.why: The idea of fitting turns from the occasion to the purpose, and a tool that does not fit its job is called inappropriate.
senses.whyCN: 「合适」的对象从场合转向目的，配不上任务的办法就叫不恰当。

senses.title: Not suitable for someone
senses.titleCN: 不适宜某人的；不适龄的
senses.definition: not suitable for a particular person because of age, rank, or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 因年龄、职位或关系而不适合特定的人
senses.example: That film is inappropriate for young children.
senses.exampleCN: 那部电影不适合年幼的孩子。
senses.why: Beyond occasions and methods, the word can measure a match between a thing and the person who receives it.
senses.whyCN: 除了场合和办法，这个词也用来衡量事物与接受者本人是否相配。

intro.en: Inappropriate is the negative in- plus appropriate, from Latin ad- plus proprius, ones own, through the verb appropriare.
intro.cn: inappropriate 是否定前缀 in- 加 appropriate；appropriate 来自拉丁语 ad- 加 proprius（自己的），经由动词 appropriare。

items.en: Proprius means ones own, personal, and proper to something.
items.cn: proprius 意为自己的、个人的、专属于某物的。

items.en: Appropriare means to make something ones own or to fit it to a use.
items.cn: appropriare 意为把某物归为己有或使之合用。

items.en: The past participle appropriatus means made suitable or taken over.
items.cn: 过去分词 appropriatus 意为「使之合宜的」或「被占用的」。

items.en: English appropriate first names something fitting, and later goods set aside for a use.
items.cn: 英语 appropriate 先指合宜之物，后指留作特定用途的财物。

items.en: A negated form with in- appears, meaning not fitting the case.
items.cn: 加否定前缀 in- 的形式出现，表示不适合当时情形。

items.en: Modern English uses inappropriate for words, behaviour, methods, and age labels.
items.cn: 现代英语用 inappropriate 评价言语、行为、方法与年龄分级。

note.en: Inappropriate pairs with proper and appropriate through Latin proprius, and neighbors words such as unsuitable and improper.
note.cn: inappropriate 通过拉丁语 proprius 与 proper、appropriate 同源，与 unsuitable、improper 等词意义相邻。

entries.definition: right or suitable for the situation
correct or fitting for the purpose
a quality of a thing, or something owned
entries.definitionCN: 性质；财产（与 appropriate 同源，并非只是拼写相近）

entries.definition: not right for a person or situation
not following accepted rules or manners
not polite or proper for the occasion

normalIntro.en: Inappropriate asks one question about any thing: does it fit this setting, this job, this person?
normalIntro.cn: inappropriate 只问一件事：这东西配不配这个场合、这份工作、这个人？

normal.en: Inappropriate behaviour is the most common pattern, especially in workplace rules.
normal.cn: 不当行为是最常见的搭配，在单位规章里尤其多见。

normal.en: Inappropriate for someone means the thing does not suit that person.
normal.cn: inappropriate for 某人，就是这东西不适合那个人。

normal.en: The adverb inappropriately appears in formal reviews and complaints.
normal.cn: 副词 inappropriately 多见于正式评论与投诉。

normal.en: Compare suitable: the negated in- is the same as in inaccurate and incomplete.
normal.cn: 对比 suitable：这个否定 in- 与 inaccurate、incomplete 的 in- 相同。

normal.en: The root proprius, ones own, also hides in proper and property.
normal.cn: 词根 proprius（自己的）也藏在 proper 与 property 里。

abstract.en: Picture a formal coat worn to a summer wedding.
abstract.cn: 想象盛夏婚礼上有人穿着厚外套。

abstract.en: Imagine a hammer used where a scalpel is needed.
abstract.cn: 想象该用手术刀的时候却拿起了锤子。

abstract.en: Think of a senior joke told to a room of small children.
abstract.cn: 想象在坐满小孩的屋里讲成年人的笑话。

examples.en: The manager gave the intern inappropriate advice.
examples.cn: 经理给了实习生不恰当的建议。

examples.en: Using that tone with a client is inappropriate.
examples.cn: 用那种语气和客户说话是不合适的。

examples.en: Some of the scenes are inappropriate for a family audience.
examples.cn: 其中一些场景不适合家庭观众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 appropri 挨特」——在「恰当的」前面加个不，就成了不合场合；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ ad-（向）+ proprius（自己的，合适的）→ appropriatus（使之合宜的）→ 英语 appropriate → 加 in- 得 inappropriate，核心义「配不上当时的人与事」。

sensesIntro.en: Inappropriate judges a thing against its situation first, then against the task, and finally against the person receiving it.
sensesIntro.cn: inappropriate 先对照场合评判，再对照任务评判，最后对照接受者评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick winter coat at a summer wedding.
core.cn: 核心意象：盛夏婚礼上的一件厚羽绒服。

branches.en: Failing to suit the occasion is the first sense.
branches.cn: 不合场合是第一个义项。

branches.en: Failing to suit the task is the second sense.
branches.cn: 不合任务的办法是第二个义项。

branches.en: Failing to suit a person is the third sense.
branches.cn: 不合特定的人是第三个义项。

branches.en: Both a wrong joke and a wrong method are things out of place.
branches.cn: 不合场的笑话和不得当的方法都属「放错了位」。

branches.en: Judging an occasion and judging a viewer use the same test of fit.
branches.cn: 评判场合与评判观众用的是同一套「配不配」的标准。

intro.en: Inappropriate is in- plus appropriate, which is built on Latin proprius, ones own.
intro.cn: inappropriate 是 in- 加 appropriate，而 appropriate 建立在拉丁语 proprius（自己的）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius gives the idea of what belongs to a thing, and appropriare gives the idea of fitting.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 提供「属于某物」的观念，appropriare 提供「使之合宜」的观念。

items.example: The prefix in- turns appropriate into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 appropriate 变成反义。

items.example: The prefix ad- is absorbed in appropriare, which has a doubled p.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 并入 appropriare，拼写中出现了双写 p。

items.meaning: ones own, proper to a thing
items.example: Proprius gives the idea of what fits its owner.
items.exampleCN: proprius 提供「属于自己、与之相称」的意思。

items.meaning: to make ones own or fit for a use
items.example: Appropriare turns proprius into a verb of fitting.
items.exampleCN: appropriare 把 proprius 变成表示「使合宜」的动词。

items.example: Appropriate is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: appropriate 是这个词族的基础。

items.example: Inappropriate negates appropriate.
items.exampleCN: inappropriate 否定 appropriate。

items.example: Proper comes down the same French path from proprius.
items.exampleCN: proper 经由法语从 proprius 一路传来。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate ends appropriate and intimate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 出现在 appropriate 与 intimate 末尾。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inappropriately.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 inappropriately。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms inappropriateness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 inappropriateness。

latinEntries.meaning: to fit or take as ones own

definition_zh: 为……举行就职典礼；为……举行落成仪式；开创；开启
definition_en: to put a person or an institution formally into office, to open a new place with a ceremony, or to mark the beginning of something new
core_image: 预言家把一只手放在新官肩上，宣布新任期开始
scene: 学校的新图书馆刚刚落成，礼堂里挤满了师生，来宾正在剪彩。The guests inaugurated the new library with a short speech and a ribbon cut.
sceneCN: 这里 inaugurate 是「为……举行落成仪式」（第 2 个义项：举行启用仪式）；句意：来宾用简短的讲话和剪彩为新图书馆举行了落成仪式。

pos.zh: 为……举行就职典礼；为……举行落成仪式；开创；开启

collocations.zh: 为新建筑举行落成典礼

derivatives.zh: 由动词加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「就职典礼；落成典礼；开端」
由主语干加后缀 -al 构成，义为「就职的；开幕的；首次的」

senses.title: To put into office with a ceremony
senses.definition: to swear in a new leader or official in a formal public ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在正式公开的典礼上让新的领导人或官员宣誓就职
senses.example: The new prime minister was inaugurated on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 新首相在周一宣誓就职。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to take auspices, and Roman augurs read the omens before an official took power, so the word grew up around the moment a person enters office.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是「占卜吉凶」，罗马占卜师在官员就任前要先看预兆，所以这个词天然长在「一个人开始掌权」的那一刻。

senses.title: To open a place with a ceremony
senses.definition: to open a new building, service, or public place officially with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 用仪式正式启用新的建筑、设施或公共场所
senses.example: The mayor will inaugurate the new airport next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 市长明年春天将为新机场举行落成典礼。
senses.why: If the auspices were read for a new office holder, they were equally read for a new temple or bridge, so inaugurate came to cover any place formally opened for use.
senses.whyCN: 既然任职要看吉兆，建一座新神庙或新桥同样要看，于是 inaugurate 也覆盖了任何被正式启用的场所。

senses.title: To begin something new
senses.definition: to mark the official beginning of a new period, policy, or way of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个新时期、新政策或新做法的正式开端
senses.example: The discovery inaugurated a new age of medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现开启了医学的新时代。
senses.why: A solemn pledge marks a fresh start, and the word extends from the person or place being opened to the period that opens with it.
senses.whyCN: 庄严的仪式宣告一个全新开始，这个词便从被启用的人或场所，延伸到随之开启的那段时间。

senses.title: To introduce something into use
senses.definition: to start using a plan, system, or product in an official and public way
senses.definitionCN: 以公开而正式的方式开始使用某项计划、制度或产品
senses.example: The company inaugurated a four-day working week in June.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在六月开始实行四天工作周。
senses.why: To use an official ceremony for a policy is to give it a public start, which is the practical branch of the core image.
senses.whyCN: 为一项政策举行正式仪式，就是给它一个公开的开端，这是核心意象最务实的一条分支。

senses.title: To take a first ride or a debut
senses.definition: to make a first journey or appearance, as with a ship, train, or flight in American use
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指船舶、列车或航班的首次航行或首次亮相
senses.example: The first flight to the island was inaugurated last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 飞往这座岛的首次航班去年夏天开通。
senses.why: A first trip deserves a first celebration, so American transport language borrowed the ceremonial start for a maiden voyage.
senses.whyCN: 首航值得最隆重的庆祝，于是美式交通用语借用了这个仪式性的「开端」去指第一次航行。

intro.en: Inaugurate comes from Latin inaugurare, meaning to take omens with augury, at root a matter of watching birds and other signs.
intro.cn: inaugurate 来自拉丁语 inaugurare（以占卜取兆），词根本义与观察飞鸟等征兆有关。

items.en: The verb augurare means to take omens, from augur, a bird-divining priest.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 augurare 意为取兆，源自 augur（观鸟占卜的祭司）。

items.en: Inaugurare adds in- and means to consult the augurs, then to install someone with such rites.
items.cn: inaugurare 加上前缀 in-，意为请占卜师问卜，进而指以这套仪式使某人就职。

items.en: Augurium names the augur office and the signs themselves; its link to avis, bird, is often suggested.
items.cn: augurium 指占卜师之职与所见的征兆；它与 avis（鸟）的关联常被提出。

items.en: Inauguratio names the act of consecration carried out by the augurs.
items.cn: 拉丁语 inauguratio 指由占卜师主持的祝圣之举。

items.en: English takes the verb from the Latin stem, first for solemn dedication, later for taking office.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干借入这个动词，早期指庄严奉献，后来指就任。

items.en: Modern usage widens from officials and buildings to any formal beginning.
items.cn: 现代用法从官员与建筑扩展为任何正式的开端。

note.en: Inaugurate shares its root with augur, auspices, and inaugurate family nouns, and sits near ordinary opening verbs.
note.cn: inaugurate 与 augur、auspices 以及表「就职、开幕」的派生词同根，并与普通的「开启」动词相邻。

entries.definition: an ancient priest who read omens, or to be a sign of something
entries.definitionCN: 古代读兆的占卜师；也作动词，预示

entries.definition: the reading of omens, especially from birds
a ceremony introducing someone into office
to start something new and public
to set a process going
to admit someone to office by an oath

normalIntro.en: Inaugurate carries the old bird-omen root augur: to begin something official was once to ask the gods for a sign.
normalIntro.cn: inaugurate 保留了古老的「观鸟取兆」词根 augur：让某件大事正式开始，原本就是先向神询问征兆。

normal.en: The noun inauguration and the adjective inaugural both drop the verb ending.
normal.cn: 名词 inauguration 与形容词 inaugural 都只保留动词词干。

normal.en: An inaugural speech is a first speech given at a start of office.
normal.cn: inaugural speech 就是就职时第一次发表的演讲。

normal.en: To inaugurate a building is to open it with a ceremony, not to finish building it.
normal.cn: inaugurate a building 是举行启用典礼，而不是建完房子。

normal.en: Inaugurate a new era means to begin a new period in public.
normal.cn: inaugurate a new era 指公开开启一个新时期。

normal.en: Compare launch and initiate: both can begin things, but inaugurate keeps a ceremonial air.
normal.cn: 对比 launch 与 initiate：它们都能表示开始，但 inaugurate 更带仪式感。

abstract.en: Picture a bird flying across the sky while a new leader waits for the sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟飞过天空，新领导人正在等待那个预兆。

abstract.en: Imagine a white ribbon cut in front of a brand-new door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇崭新的门前，白丝带被剪断。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy book opening to its very first page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书翻到第一页。

examples.en: The university inaugurated its new science centre in March.
examples.cn: 这所大学在三月为新科学中心举行了落成典礼。

examples.en: A year of record sales inaugurated a new phase for the company.
examples.cn: 创纪录销售的一年为公司开启了新阶段。

examples.en: The mayor gave an inaugural address after the ceremony.
examples.cn: 典礼之后，市长发表了就职演说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一诺给瑞特」——一诺千金地给人授职、给门剪彩；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 in-（进入）+ augur（占卜师、看兆）→ inaugurare（取兆、奉神意使就职）→ 英语 inaugurate，核心义「以正式的征兆与仪式让某事物开始」。

sensesIntro.en: Inaugurate starts at a person taking office, widens to a place being opened, and then to any period, policy, or first journey being begun.
sensesIntro.cn: inaugurate 从人正式就职开始，扩展到场所被正式启用，再扩展到任何时期、政策或首航的开始。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a priest reads the birds and declares that a new beginning is blessed.
core.cn: 核心意象：祭司看完飞鸟，宣布新的开始已被祝福。

branches.en: A leader enters office, the first public sense.
branches.cn: 领导人走马上任，是最先公开的义项。

branches.en: A place opens for use, the building sense.
branches.cn: 场所被正式启用，是建筑场景的义项。

branches.en: A period opens, the abstract beginning sense.
branches.cn: 一个时期被开启，是抽象的开端义项。

branches.en: A new building and a first flight are both first official uses.
branches.cn: 新楼落成与首航开通都是第一次正式使用。

branches.en: A new era and a new policy both begin with deliberate ceremony.
branches.cn: 新时代与新政策都以刻意的仪式同时开始。

intro.en: Inaugurate is built from the Latin in- prefix, the augur root meaning diviner, and the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: inaugurate 由拉丁语前缀 in-、表示占卜师的 augur 词根以及动词词尾 -ate 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin augur names the priest who reads bird signs, and inaugurare means to install with such signs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 augur 指观鸟取兆的祭司，inaugurare 意为凭这些征兆使就职。

items.example: The augur watched the birds before every decision.
items.exampleCN: 每逢大事，占卜师都要先看飞鸟。

items.example: Augurium names the signs themselves.
items.exampleCN: augurium 指征兆本身。

items.example: The prefix in- turns a reading into an act of installing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把「看兆」变成「使就职」。

items.example: Inaugurare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: inaugurare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ate carries the verb sense of the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 承载了拉丁词干的动词含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms inauguration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 inauguration。

items.example: The suffix -al forms inaugural.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 inaugural。

items.example: Auspices grew from the same bird-watching word as augur.
items.exampleCN: auspices 与 augur 同出「观鸟取兆」这一词源。

items.example: Augury keeps the priestly sense in English.
items.exampleCN: augury 在英语中保留了祭司的占卜含义。

definition_zh: 天生的；与生俱来的；固有的
definition_en: present in a person or animal from birth and not gained through learning or experience
core_image: 婴儿一落地就紧紧握住大人的手指，不用人教
scene: 老园丁对小孙子说，这孩子从会走路起就蹲在花圃边看虫子，从来没人教过他。The boy has an inborn talent for plants.
sceneCN: 这里 inborn 是「生来就有的」（第 1 个义项：生来就有的）；句意：这个男孩有与生俱来的植物天赋。

pos.zh: 天生的；与生俱来的；固有的

derivatives.zh: 与 borne 同出于 bear 一词，义为「出生；诞生」，可见 inborn 的「生来」底色
由词根 borne 的动词原形构成，义为「生育；承受」，它是 inborn 的后半部分

senses.title: Present from birth
senses.definition: existing in a person or animal from the moment of birth rather than being learned
senses.definitionCN: 从出生那一刻起就存在于人或动物身上，而非后天学来的
senses.example: Cats show an inborn fear of snakes.
senses.exampleCN: 猫对蛇有天生的恐惧。
senses.why: The word is literally in plus born, so it names whatever a creature carries with it out of the womb.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在……之中出生」，因此指生物从出生起就随身带着的东西。

senses.title: Built into a natural system
senses.definition: part of the natural arrangement of living things and not produced by people
senses.definitionCN: 属于生物的自然构造，而非由人为制造
senses.example: An inborn clock helps birds know when to fly south.
senses.exampleCN: 一种天生的时钟帮鸟类判断何时南飞。
senses.why: If something is in your make-up at birth, it belongs to the design of your body, which reaches beyond people to animals and plant life.
senses.whyCN: 若某物在出生时就已存在于身体构造里，它就属于身体的天然设计，这层意思从人延伸到动物乃至植物。

senses.title: Inherent in a group or thing
senses.definition: belonging to a group, place, or thing as part of its own nature
senses.definitionCN: 作为某群体、地点或事物自身本性的一部分而属于它
senses.example: The village has an inborn suspicion of strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座村子对外来人有种固有的戒备。
senses.why: The birth image shifts from a single body to a whole community, whose habits feel as natural as the way it was born.
senses.whyCN: 「出生」的画面从单个身体挪到一个群体，群体的习性便像它生来的样子一样自然。

senses.title: Born as a native quality
senses.definition: used of a quality that someone has always shown, as if it came with the birth
senses.definitionCN: 指某人一直表现出来的品质，仿佛伴随出生而来
senses.example: She has an inborn grace that no training could copy.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种生来的优雅，任何训练都模仿不来。
senses.why: This is the mildly approving branch: the trait feels native and unfaked, as if it were printed on the person at birth.
senses.whyCN: 这是略带赞许的一支：这种品质显得浑然天成，仿佛一个人出生时就被印了上去。

intro.en: Inborn is a transparent English compound of in and born, the past participle of bear, and it has meant present at birth since the Middle English period.
intro.cn: inborn 是 in 与 born（bear 的过去分词）构成的透明英语复合词，自中古英语时期起就表示「出生时即具备」。

items.en: Boren, the past participle of beran, means carried or brought forth.
items.cn: 古英语 boren 是 beran（承载、生育）的过去分词，意为「被带来、被生下」。

items.en: Beboren means born and provides the earliest in-born structure.
items.cn: 古英语 be-boren 意为「生来的」，是最早的「在……出生」结构。

items.en: Inborn appears as an adjective describing qualities present at birth.
items.cn: 中古英语中 inborn 作为形容词出现，描述出生时就具备的品质。

items.en: Writers start using inborn for instincts and natural settings as well as people.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，写作者开始用 inborn 来形容本能与自然环境，而不仅限于人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word mostly for traits and abilities and pairs it often with talent or instinct.
items.cn: 现代英语仍主要用它指特质与能力，并常与 talent、instinct 搭配。

note.en: Inborn looks close to the birth words born and inbred, and it sits near the ordinary words for natural traits.
note.cn: inborn 与表示「出生」的 born、inbred 形近，并与日常表达「天然特质」的词相邻。

entries.definition: brought into life, the past participle of bear
entries.definitionCN: 出生的；天生的（bear 的过去分词）

entries.definition: existing from birth, or produced by breeding within a small group
built into a thing as a fixed part of it
entries.definitionCN: 内置的；固有的（只是构词相似，词根来自 build，与 inborn 词源不同）

entries.definition: present from birth as part of the nature of a person
entries.definitionCN: 天生的；固有的（更书面，多用于心理学与哲学）

entries.definition: existing as a natural and permanent part of something
done or felt without thought

normalIntro.en: Inborn is a two-part English word: in, meaning inside, plus born, the moment when life starts.
normalIntro.cn: inborn 是一个两部分合起来的英语词：in（在……之中）加上 born（出生），也就是你人生最初那一刻发生在你身上的事。

normal.en: Born is the past participle of bear, so inborn literally means born in.
normal.cn: born 是 bear 的过去分词，所以 inborn 字面就是「生来带来的」。

normal.en: Pair it with talent or instinct: an inborn talent, an inborn instinct.
normal.cn: 它常与 talent 或 instinct 搭配：inborn talent 天赋，inborn instinct 本能。

normal.en: Its near formal twin is innate, and both mean present from birth.
normal.cn: 它的近义书面词是 innate，两者都表示出生时就具备。

normal.en: If a skill was taught, it is learned and not inborn.
normal.cn: 如果一项技能是被教会的，那它就是学来的，而不是 inborn。

normal.en: Compare inborn with inbred: same pattern, but inbred is not used for talent.
normal.cn: 对比 inborn 与 inbred：构词相同，但 inbred 不用来形容才能。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn hand closing around a finger on the first day.
abstract.cn: 想象出生第一天，一只小手就紧紧握住大人的手指。

abstract.en: Imagine a seed that already knows which way to grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子早已知道该往哪个方向生长。

abstract.en: Think of a family habit passed down so long it feels like a birthmark.
abstract.cn: 想象一种传了很久的家风，久得像出生就带来的胎记。

examples.en: Some musicians seem to have an inborn sense of rhythm.
examples.cn: 有些音乐家似乎天生就有节奏感。

examples.en: Curiosity is not inborn in every child, but it can be encouraged.
examples.cn: 好奇心并非每个孩子都天生具备，但可以被激发。

examples.en: The birds follow an inborn map long before they have ever flown south.
examples.cn: 这些鸟从未飞去过南方，却早已遵循着一张与生俱来的地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬棒」——天生就硬朗、生来就是好料的棒子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 in-（在……之中）+ born（bear 的过去分词，意为「生育、带来」）→ inborn（在出生之中带来的），核心义「随出生一同带来、不用后天学」。

sensesIntro.en: Inborn first describes traits carried from birth, then natural clocks and systems in animals, and finally qualities felt to be fixed in a group or a person.
sensesIntro.cn: inborn 先指从出生带有的特质，再指动物体内的天然机制，最后指被看作固定在群体或某人身上的品质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newborn hand grips a finger without being taught.
core.cn: 核心意象：新生儿没人教就会紧握手指。

branches.en: A feature present at birth is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 出生即有的特征是基本义项。

branches.en: A natural system inside animals is the biological sense.
branches.cn: 动物体内的天然机制是生物学义项。

branches.en: A fixed group habit is the social sense.
branches.cn: 群体固定的习性是社会义项。

branches.en: A talent and a grace both feel as if printed on the person at birth.
branches.cn: 天赋与优雅都像是出生时就印在人身上的。

branches.en: Bird clocks and village habits are both patterns no one taught.
branches.cn: 鸟的时钟与村子的习俗都是没人教就有的模式。

intro.en: Inborn is a native English compound of the prefix in- and the participle born, with no Latin affixes of its own.
intro.cn: inborn 是英语本族复合词，由前缀 in- 与分词 born 组成，本身不含拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor, but its meaning matches the Latin-rooted borrowing innate, built on in- and nasci, to be born.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，但它的意思与拉丁语源的借词 innate 相当，后者由 in- 与 nasci（出生）构成。

items.example: The prefix in- marks what is inside a creature from the start.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 标出生物从一开始就内在具备的东西。

items.example: Born is the past participle of bear.
items.exampleCN: born 是 bear 的过去分词。

items.meaning: to carry or to give birth
items.example: Bear supplies the second half of inborn.
items.exampleCN: bear 提供了 inborn 的后半部分。

items.example: Birth comes from the same root as borne.
items.exampleCN: birth 与 borne 同根。

items.example: Innate borrows Latin in- plus nasci.
items.exampleCN: innate 借自拉丁语 in- 加 nasci。

items.example: Inherent uses Latin in- plus haerere, to stick.
items.exampleCN: inherent 用拉丁语 in- 加 haerere（黏附）。

items.meaning: belonging to a place or person by birth
items.example: Native comes from Latin nasci, to be born.
items.exampleCN: native 也来自拉丁语 nasci（出生）。

items.meaning: existing from birth, or bred among relatives
items.example: Inbred copies the in plus participle pattern.
items.exampleCN: inbred 沿用「in 加分词」的构词方式。

items.meaning: present from birth, as of a condition
items.example: Congenital is the medical near twin of inborn.
items.exampleCN: congenital 是 inborn 在医学上的近似词。

definition_zh: 收件箱（办公室中收文件的小筐）；电子邮箱的收件箱；待处理事项的清单
definition_en: a tray on a desk for papers that have to be dealt with, or the electronic folder on a computer where arriving mail is kept
core_image: 办公桌角上那只木框小筐，早上又堆满了新的文件
scene: 早晨刚到办公室，桌上那只小木筐里已经塞满了昨天的单据，还压着一张便条。A thick pile of letters was waiting in his inbox.
sceneCN: 这里 inbox 是「收文件的筐」（第 1 个义项：办公室收文件的筐）；句意：他的收件筐里已经等着厚厚一叠信件。

pos.zh: 收件箱（办公用筐）；电子邮箱收件箱；待处理事项清单

collocations.zh: 清空收件箱；处理完邮件

derivatives.zh: inbox 的镜像词，把 in 换成 out，义为「发件箱；待发文件筐」
由 mail（邮件）+ box（箱）构成，义为「信箱；邮箱」，是 inbox 的上位词之一
inbox 的后半部分，义为「箱；盒」，单独使用也可表示信箱

senses.title: A desk tray for incoming papers
senses.definition: a shallow open box kept on a desk for letters and papers that come in and wait to be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 桌上用来存放送来、尚待处理的信件和文件的浅口小筐
senses.example: Leave the invoice in my inbox, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请把发票放在我的收件筐里。
senses.why: The word is simply in plus box, the container for what flows inward, so the oldest sense names the physical tray on an office desk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 in 加 box，即「朝里流的箱子」，所以最早的义项就是办公桌上那只实体小筐。

senses.title: An electronic folder for new mail
senses.definition: the folder in an email program or online account where new messages are received
senses.definitionCN: 电子邮件程序或网络账号中用来接收新邮件的文件夹
senses.example: The confirmation code should be in your inbox within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 确认码应该会在一分钟内到你的收件箱。
senses.why: When letters became messages, the tray for incoming post moved onto the screen unchanged in name and purpose.
senses.whyCN: 当信件变成讯息，那只「收新东西的筐」几乎原封不动地搬到了屏幕上，名字和用途都没变。

senses.title: A list of things to handle
senses.definition: a personal list of tasks, requests, or ideas that have not yet been sorted out
senses.definitionCN: 尚未安排处理的任务、请求或想法的个人清单
senses.example: Every Friday she empties her inbox into three short tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 每周五她把待办清单上的事压缩成三件小任务。
senses.why: In time-management practice the tray becomes a metaphor for anything waiting for a decision, such as tasks or ideas.
senses.whyCN: 在时间管理方法里，那只筐成了隐喻，指一切等待被决定的事，比如任务或点子。

senses.title: A device feed for arriving messages
senses.definition: the area on a phone, app, or game service that collects incoming messages, alerts, or gifts
senses.definitionCN: 手机、应用或游戏服务端用来收集新消息、提醒或礼物的区域
senses.example: Special event rewards appear in the game inbox.
senses.exampleCN: 活动奖励会出现在游戏的收件区。
senses.why: Any stream of incoming things needs a landing place, and digital products reuse the box image for alerts and rewards as well as mail.
senses.whyCN: 任何朝里送来的一串东西都需要落脚处，数字产品便把「箱子」这个画面借去装提醒和奖励。

intro.en: Inbox is a modern English compound of in and box, invented for office paperwork and later stretched to email; its earliest recorded English use is from the twentieth century.
intro.cn: inbox 是 in 与 box 的现代英语复合词，为办公文书而造，后来又延伸到电子邮件；英语文献中最早的书面用例出现在二十世纪。

items.en: Buxus names the box tree, giving Latin buxis and then English box for a container.
items.cn: 拉丁语 buxus 指黄杨木，衍生出 buxis，再进入英语成为 box（箱子）。

items.en: Box appears in Old English mainly for the wooden box of the box tree.
items.cn: 古英语 box 主要指黄杨木制成的木盒。

items.en: Inbox enters office English in the twentieth century for a tray of paper work still to be done.
items.cn: 二十世纪，inbox 进入办公室语言，指盛放待办文书的小筐。

items.en: Computer mail systems take over the tray word for a folder of arriving messages.
items.cn: 二十世纪七八十年代，计算机邮件系统借用了这个文件筐词，指存放来件的文件夹。

items.en: Today inbox covers email, apps, and personal task queues, and is a verb in the phrase to inbox someone.
items.cn: 如今 inbox 覆盖电子邮件、应用与个人任务清单，并可用作动词表示给某人发站内私信。

note.en: Inbox looks like the outbox and mailbox words built on the same box root, and it sits near the other words for where messages and post arrive.
note.cn: inbox 与同出 box 词根的 outbox、mailbox 形近，并与表示「消息与信件到达处」的其他词相邻。

entries.definition: a tray or folder for items waiting to be sent
a box where letters are delivered
a container with straight sides
a slot or box in a door or wall for letters
a bag for post, or the letters someone receives
recorded telephone messages waiting to be heard

normalIntro.en: Inbox is an open compound in plus box: the box into which things come, opposite of outbox which sends things away.
normalIntro.cn: inbox 是 in 加 box 的透明复合词：朝里进的箱子，与朝外发的 outbox 正好相反。

normal.en: The stem box gives the plural inboxes, spelled with an e to keep the sound soft.
normal.cn: 词干 box 带来复数 inboxes，要加 e 才保持读音。

normal.en: Outbox is the mirror image: letters go out rather than come in.
normal.cn: outbox 是镜像词：信件是发出去而不是收进来。

normal.en: To sign up for updates is to invite notices into your inbox.
normal.cn: 订阅更新，就是邀请通知进入你的收件箱。

normal.en: In time management, an inbox holds anything still waiting for a decision.
normal.cn: 在时间管理中，inbox 装着一切仍等待做决定的事。

normal.en: Compare mailbox: a mailbox is for post delivery, an inbox is for mail you already received.
normal.cn: 对比 mailbox：mailbox 指投递用的信箱，inbox 指已经收到的邮件存放处。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden tray filling up before you have even sat down.
abstract.cn: 想象你还没坐下，木筐就已经堆满了。

abstract.en: Imagine a screen door that only lets messages in, never out.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只让消息进、不让消息出的门。

abstract.en: Think of a basket that never stays empty for long.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永远空不了多久的篮子。

examples.en: I found the contract in my inbox this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我在收件筐里找到了那份合同。

examples.en: Her inbox was full of complaints after the delay.
examples.cn: 延误之后，她的电子收件箱塞满了投诉。

examples.en: He moves every note from his inbox into a dated file.
examples.cn: 他把收件筐里的每张便条都归进按日期归档的卷宗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬盒子」——一个硬邦邦的盒子，专门收进来的东西；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 in（进入）+ box（箱子，源自拉丁语 buxus「黄杨木」）→ inbox（朝里进的箱子），核心义「接收来件、尚待处理的地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Inbox begins as a box for incoming paper, then becomes the email folder, then a metaphor for tasks waiting, and finally the message area on any device.
sensesIntro.cn: inbox 先是收进纸质文件的小筐，再成为电子邮件收件箱，然后是待办事项的隐喻，最后泛指任何设备上的消息收件区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray on a desk that fills with papers as they arrive.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上那只随来件而不断堆满的筐。

branches.en: The desk tray is the literal first sense.
branches.cn: 办公桌上的小筐是字面意义上的第一义项。

branches.en: The email folder is the digital transfer of the tray.
branches.cn: 电子收件箱是小筐移到数字世界的结果。

branches.en: The task list is the metaphorical extension.
branches.cn: 待办清单是隐喻性的延伸。

branches.en: A paper tray and an email folder both receive what must be handled next.
branches.cn: 纸质小筐与电子收件箱都接收接下来必须处理的东西。

branches.en: Mail, tasks, and app rewards are all queued for action.
branches.cn: 邮件、任务与应用奖励都被排队等候处理。

intro.en: Inbox is built from the prefix-like particle in and the noun box, and it has mirrored words like outbox.
intro.cn: inbox 由表示「进入」的 in 与名词 box 构成，并衍生出 outbox 这样的镜像词。

latinIntro.en: The box in inbox goes back to Latin buxus, the box tree, whose wood was used for small boxes.
latinIntro.cn: inbox 中的 box 可追溯到拉丁语 buxus（黄杨木），这种木料正是做小盒子的用料。

items.example: The prefix in- points the flow inward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示向内流入。

items.example: Box supplies the container image.
items.exampleCN: box 提供容器意象。

items.example: Buxus is the earliest ancestor of box.
items.exampleCN: buxus 是 box 最早的来源。

items.example: Buxis leads into English box.
items.exampleCN: buxis 进入英语成为 box。

items.example: The prefix out- makes the mirror word outbox.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 构成镜像词 outbox。

items.meaning: a tray for things to send
items.example: Outbox reverses the direction of inbox.
items.exampleCN: outbox 把 inbox 的方向反过来。

items.example: Mailbox adds the mail element to box.
items.exampleCN: mailbox 在 box 前加上表示邮件的 mail。

items.meaning: the act of sending a direct message
items.example: Inboxing is the verb side of the noun inbox.
items.exampleCN: inboxing 是名词 inbox 的动词用法。

items.example: Letterbox uses the same box pattern for post.
items.exampleCN: letterbox 沿用同样的 box 构词方式指信件。

definition_zh: 不可估量的；无法计算的；难以预料的；极大的
definition_en: too great or too many to be counted or measured
core_image: 一把算盘拨到尽头，数目仍堆得望不到边
scene: 第 一 个义项：不可估量的。看见海边的老房子被海浪一点点吞掉，房主说不出损失有多大。Watching the old house by the shore slowly swallowed by the waves, the owner could not put a figure on the incalculable loss.
sceneCN: 这里的 incalculable 是「不可估量的」（第 1 个义项：大到无法计算或衡量）；句意：看着海边的老房子一点点被海浪吞掉，房主无法为该无法估量的损失给出一个数字。

pos.zh: 不可估量的；无法计算的
难以预料的；不确定的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词「incalculable」加词尾「-ly」构成，义为「不可估量地」
去掉否定前缀「in-」后，义为「可计算的；可预估的」
基础动词，义为「计算；估算」，是这个形容词的源头
由动词「calculate」加名词词尾「-ion」构成，义为「计算；推算」
同一词根的名词，义为「微积分；结石」，最初指用于计数的石子

senses.title: Too great to be measured
senses.definition: so great in size, amount, or value that it cannot be counted or measured
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、规模或价值上大到无法计算或衡量
senses.example: The war caused incalculable damage to the old city.
senses.exampleCN: 那场战争给这座古城造成了无法估量的破坏。
senses.why: The Latin prefix in- adds a negative, and calculare means to reckon with counters, so the word names what the counters can never finish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 表示否定，calculare 意为用小石子计数，所以这个词指计数者永远数不完的东西。

senses.title: Impossible to predict
senses.definition: impossible to know or predict in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先无法知道或预测的
senses.example: The incalculable effects of the new policy will show up years later.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新政策难以预料的影响要多年后才会显现。
senses.why: If an outcome cannot be reckoned in advance, it also cannot be predicted, so the counting sense stretches to the future.
