senses.whyCN: 如果结果无法事先推算，也就无法预测，于是计数的含义延伸到了未来。

senses.title: Impossible to compute in principle
senses.definition: not able to be worked out by any calculation or method
senses.definitionCN: 在原理上无法用计算或任何方法求出的
senses.example: In mathematics, some quantities are incalculable even in principle.
senses.exampleCN: 在数学中，有些量即使在原理上也无法计算。
senses.why: In science the word keeps its literal power and marks a limit that no method can cross.
senses.whyCN: 在科学语境中，这个词保留了字面的力量，标出一个任何方法都无法跨越的界限。

senses.title: Capable of being computed
senses.definition: able to be calculated or worked out precisely
senses.definitionCN: 能够被精确计算或推算出来的
senses.example: The calculable risks were tiny compared with the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 相比其余部分，这些可计算的风险很小。
senses.why: The prefix in- can be dropped, and the bare base calculable marks exactly the area where counting still works.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 可以去掉，剩下的 calculable 正好指计数仍然有效的范围。

senses.title: An extremely large number
senses.definition: existing in numbers too large to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 数量多到无法计数的
senses.example: An incalculable number of stars fill the night sky.
senses.exampleCN: 多得无法计数的星星布满夜空。
senses.why: When the quantity of things is beyond counting, the same word is used for sheer abundance.
senses.whyCN: 当事物的数量超出可计数的范围时，同一个词就用来表示数量极其庞大。

senses.title: Beyond all reckoning in value
senses.definition: having a worth so high that no price can express it
senses.definitionCN: 价值高到任何价格都无法表达的
senses.example: The library is of incalculable value to scholars.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆对学者们有着不可估量的价值。
senses.why: Value is one more thing that counters cannot capture, so pricelessness becomes a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: 价值也是计数抓不住的东西，所以「无价」成了自然延伸出来的意思。

senses.title: Unpredictable in mood or behaviour
senses.definition: unpredictable in temper or behaviour, so hard to rely on
senses.definitionCN: 性情或行为无法预测，因此难以依靠的
senses.example: His incalculable temper frightened even his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他难以捉摸的脾气连朋友都害怕。
senses.why: People can also fail to be reckoned, so an unpredictable temper comes to be called incalculable.
senses.whyCN: 人对自己也常常无法推算，于是难以预测的脾气也被称作 incalculable。

senses.title: A balance sheet that cannot be drawn
senses.definition: describing debts or accounts too tangled to be settled
senses.definitionCN: 形容债务或账目混乱到无法结清的
senses.example: After years of borrowing, the family was left with incalculable debts.
senses.exampleCN: 借了多年之后，这家人欠下了无法结清的债务。
senses.why: Money was the original thing counted, so even a ledger that can never be closed returns to the same image.
senses.whyCN: 钱本来就是要数的东西，所以连一本永远结不清的账目也回到同一个画面。

intro.en: Incalculable joins the negative prefix in- to calculable, which comes from Latin calculare, to reckon with small stones.
intro.cn: incalculable 由否定前缀 in- 加 calculable 构成，后者来自拉丁语 calculare（用小石子计算）。

items.en: Calx means a small stone or pebble used as a counter.
items.cn: calx 意为用作筹码的小石子。

items.en: Calculare means to reckon or count with such stones.
items.cn: calculare 意为用这种石子推算、计数。

items.en: Calculus, a small pebble, becomes the Latin word for reckoning.
items.cn: calculus 本意小石子，后来成为拉丁语中表示「推算」的词。

items.en: Calculate enters English as a verb for counting and reckoning.
items.cn: calculate 作为表示计数与推算的动词进入英语。

items.en: Calculable appears, and the negated incalculable follows it.
items.cn: calculable 出现，否定形式 incalculable 随后出现。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to damage, value, and future effects.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到损害、价值与未来影响。

note.en: Incalculable sits at the edge of the counting family, next to calculable and calculi, and near words for immeasurable size.
note.cn: incalculable 处在「计数」这一词族的边缘，与 calculable、calculus 相邻，也靠近表示「无法测量」的词。

entries.definition: able to be worked out by counting
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根，去掉否定前缀后表示「可计算的」

entries.definition: to work out an amount by counting
entries.definitionCN: 计算；核算，是这个形容词的源头动词

entries.definition: to keep eggs, or a disease, warm until they develop
entries.definitionCN: 孵化；潜伏，与 incalculable 只是开头几个字母相近，词源不同

entries.definition: too large to be measured
too precious to be given a value
too many to be counted

normalIntro.en: Incalculable is the word for what the counters fail to finish: in- says not, calculable says it could be reckoned.
normalIntro.cn: incalculable 指计数者永远数不完的东西：in- 表示「不」，calculable 表示「本来可以推算」。

normal.en: The prefix in- negates the whole word, so incalculable means not calculable.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 否定整个词，所以 incalculable 就是「不可计算的」。

normal.en: The base calculare comes from calx, a small stone used as a counter.
normal.cn: 词基 calculare 来自 calx，即用作筹码的小石子。

normal.en: Calculus still keeps the pebble story and now names a branch of mathematics.
normal.cn: calculus 仍保留石子的来路，如今指数学的一个分支。

normal.en: In business writing the common pair is incalculable damage or incalculable value.
normal.cn: 在商业写作中常见的搭配是 incalculable damage 或 incalculable value。

normal.en: Instead of a new word for very much, English just puts in- before a counting word.
normal.cn: 英语不用另造新词表达「非常多」，只是在一个计数的词前加上 in-。

abstract.en: Picture a heap of pebbles spilling off the table and onto the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆小石子从桌上溢出、撒了一地。

abstract.en: Imagine a weather chart with no line drawn past tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，明天之后的线完全空着。

abstract.en: Think of a calculator screen where the digits simply run out.
abstract.cn: 想象计算器的屏幕，数字一直排到再也放不下。

examples.en: The storm did incalculable damage to the coastal villages.
examples.cn: 风暴给沿海村庄造成了无法估量的损害。

examples.en: Her advice has been of incalculable value to the whole team.
examples.cn: 她的建议对整个团队具有不可估量的价值。

examples.en: The many small decisions of the committee brought consequences that remain incalculable.
examples.cn: 委员会做出的许多细微决定带来了至今仍难以预料的后果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「In卡计算伯」——连「计算伯」都卡住了，算不出来，就是不可估量的；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 calx（小石子，用作计数筹码）→ calculare（用小石子推算）→ 英语 calculate、calculable → 加否定前缀 in- 得 incalculable，核心义「数不完、算不出」。

sensesIntro.en: Incalculable moves from damage too great to measure, to effects nobody can predict, to limits set by mathematics itself.
sensesIntro.cn: incalculable 先指大得无法衡量的损害，再指无人能预料的影响，最后指数学本身设定的界限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of counting stones that never runs out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆永远数不完的计数石子。

branches.en: A loss too large to measure is the dominant everyday use.
branches.cn: 大到无法衡量的损失是日常最主要的用法。

branches.en: What cannot be reckoned cannot be foreseen either.
branches.cn: 推算不出的东西也就无法预见。

branches.en: The mathematical sense keeps the literal reading of the prefix.
branches.cn: 数学义项保留了否定前缀的字面读法。

branches.en: Great amount, great number, and great value all mean beyond the reach of counting.
branches.cn: 大的量、大的数目与大的价值都表示超出计数的范围。

branches.en: What can be reckoned, what is unpredictable, and what cannot be settled all circle the same count.
branches.cn: 可计算的、难以预测的、无法结清的，都绕着同一个「计数」打转。

intro.en: The word is built from the negative prefix in- and the Latin counting root calc-, shared by calculate and calculus.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀 in- 与拉丁语计数词根 calc- 构成，calculate 与 calculus 共享同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin calx means a pebble, and calculus means a small stone used for reckoning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calx 意为小石子，calculus 意为用来推算的小石子。

items.example: The prefix in- turns calculable into incalculable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 calculable 变成 incalculable。

items.example: Calx is the pebble behind the counting root.
items.exampleCN: calx 是计数词根背后的小石子。

items.example: Calculare gives the sense of counting.
items.exampleCN: calculare 提供计数的含义。

items.meaning: a small stone used as a counter
items.example: Calculus named the stone before it named the maths.
items.exampleCN: calculus 先指石子，后来才指数学。

items.example: Calculate is the everyday verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: calculate 是这个词族中日常使用的动词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms calculable from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 把动词变成 calculable。

items.example: Calculable is the positive base of the word.
items.exampleCN: calculable 是这个词的肯定词基。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms incalculably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 incalculably。

items.example: Incalculably describes a degree beyond counting.
items.exampleCN: incalculably 描述超出计数的程度。

items.example: Calculation names the act of the verb.
items.exampleCN: calculation 表示动词所描述的行为。

latinEntries.meaning: a small stone used as a counter

definition_zh: 使失去能力；使无行为能力的；使伤残；使不适合
definition_en: to make a person or thing unable to act or function
core_image: 一根导线被剪断，机器轰然停在半空
scene: 第 一 个义项：使失去能力。暴雨夜里，一棵倒下的树压断了电线，手机没电，呼叫救援的路也断了。A fallen tree cut the power in the storm, and with a dead phone the injured hiker was incapacitated and could not call for help.
sceneCN: 这里的 incapacitate 是「使失去能力」（第 1 个义项：使某人无法行动或运作）；句意：暴雨中一棵倒下的树切断了电力，手机又没电，受伤的徒步者因此失去了行动和求助的能力。

pos.zh: 使失去能力；使无行为能力
使伤残；使不再适合

collocations.zh: 无法工作；丧失劳动能力

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转作形容词，义为「丧失行为能力的；无力的」
由动词加名词词尾「-ion」构成，义为「丧失能力；使无能」
同族名词，义为「无能力；无资格」，多用于法律与医学
同族形容词，义为「无能力的；不能胜任的」

senses.title: To make someone unable to act
senses.definition: to make a person or group unable to act or work in the normal way
senses.definitionCN: 使人或群体无法按正常方式行动或工作
senses.example: The injury incapacitated him for several months.
senses.exampleCN: 那次受伤使他好几个月都无法行动。
senses.why: The negative prefix in- joins capacitas, capacity, so to incapacitate is to take away the room and power to act.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 接在 capacitas（容量、能力）前，所以「使失去能力」就是把行动的空间和力量夺走。

senses.title: To disable by force
senses.definition: to damage a person, machine, or vehicle so badly that it cannot function
senses.definitionCN: 严重损伤人或机器、车辆，使其无法发挥作用
senses.example: The blast incapacitated the engine of the plane.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸使飞机的发动机失去了工作能力。
senses.why: In military and medical use the word turns from general inability to a concrete disabling blow.
senses.whyCN: 在军事与医学语境中，这个词从泛指「无能」具体化为一次使人或物瘫掉的打击。

senses.title: To make legally unfit
senses.definition: to make a person legally unable to act, decide, or manage affairs
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在法律上无法行动、决策或处理事务
senses.example: The court incapacitated him from managing the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院裁定他无权管理这份遗产。
senses.why: Law borrows the word to say that a person lacks the legal capacity, the formal power to act.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词，表示一个人欠缺法律上的「能力」，也就是行动的正式资格。

senses.title: A drug or condition that stops function
senses.definition: to stop a natural function, such as breathing or muscle movement
senses.definitionCN: 使呼吸、肌肉活动等自然机能停止
senses.example: The gas incapacitated the muscles of the volunteers within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 那种气体在几秒内就让志愿者的肌肉失去了活动能力。
senses.why: When capacity means the power to function, incapacitating a muscle is to switch that power off.
senses.whyCN: 当 capacity 指发挥功能的力量时，使肌肉失去能力就是把这份力量关掉。

senses.title: To leave someone out of a role
senses.definition: to make someone unsuitable or unable to take part in something
senses.definitionCN: 使某人不再适合或无法参与某事
senses.example: His poor health incapacitated him for the demanding role.
senses.exampleCN: 他身体不好，已无法胜任这项要求很高的工作。
senses.why: Capacity also means fitness for a job, so failing capacity means being ruled out of it.
senses.whyCN: capacity 也指胜任某项工作，失去这种能力就等于被排除在外。

senses.title: To block an opponent in a game
senses.definition: to arrange the pieces or play so that an opponent can no longer make a move
senses.definitionCN: 通过走子或打法，使对手再也无法落子或出手
senses.example: With one clever move she incapacitated the whole black army.
senses.exampleCN: 她只走了一步妙棋，就让整片黑子再也动不了。
senses.why: In board games capacity becomes the freedom to move, so cutting off every move is a playful use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 在棋类中，capacity 变成「可走动的余地」，封死所有走法就是这个词的一种俏皮用法。

senses.title: To weaken the effect of something
senses.definition: to reduce the power or usefulness of something so that it hardly works
senses.definitionCN: 削弱某物的力量或效用，使其几乎不起作用
senses.example: Constant criticism had incapacitated the committee from taking decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的批评使委员会无法作出决定。
senses.why: Even an organisation can lose its capacity to act, so the word reaches abstract bodies too.
senses.whyCN: 连一个组织也可能失去行动的能力，所以这个词也能落到抽象机构身上。

senses.title: The state of being disabled
senses.definition: the condition of a person who has lost the power to work or care for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 一个人失去工作或自理能力的状态
senses.example: Insurance covered him while he was incapacitated from work.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法工作期间，保险为他提供了保障。
senses.why: The medical and legal senses settle into a noun-like state of being unable to act.
senses.whyCN: 医学与法律义项最终沉淀为一种「无法作为」的状态。

intro.en: Incapacitate is built from Latin in-, not, and capax, able to hold, the root also behind capacity and capable.
intro.cn: incapacitate 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）与 capax（能容纳、能接受）构成，capacity 与 capable 也出自同一词根。

items.en: Capere means to take or hold, the root of able to hold.
items.cn: capere 意为抓住、容纳，是「能容纳」这一含义的词根。

items.en: Capax means able to hold or receive, and capacitas means capacity.
items.cn: capax 意为能容纳、能接受，capacitas 意为容量。

items.en: Incapax negates the word, meaning unable to hold.
items.cn: incapax 是其否定形式，意为「容纳不了」。

items.en: Incapacity and incapable enter English through French forms.
items.cn: incapacity 与 incapable 经法语形式进入英语。

items.en: The verb incapacitate appears, first in legal and medical writing.
items.cn: 动词 incapacitate 出现，最初见于法律与医学写作。

items.en: Modern English extends it to machines, weapons, and games.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到机器、武器与棋局。

note.en: Incapacitate belongs to the capacity family, with capable and capacity, and is related to words that describe being disabled.
note.cn: incapacitate 属于 capacity 词族，与 capable、capacity 同宗，也与描述伤残与瘫痪的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: the power or room to hold or do something
entries.definitionCN: 同名词根词，义为「容量；能力」

entries.definition: able to do something well
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「有能力的」

entries.definition: the state of being made unable to act
entries.definitionCN: 同族名词，义为「丧失能力」

entries.definition: to make a person or machine unable to work
entries.definitionCN: 使（人或机器）丧失工作能力

entries.definition: to make the body or a part of it unable to move
to make someone or something less strong

normalIntro.en: Incapacitate is in- plus capacity: the word says that the capacity to act has been taken away.
normalIntro.cn: incapacitate 就是 in- 加 capacity：这个词说的是「行动的能力被拿走了」。

normal.en: The stem capacitas means capacity, the room to hold or do something.
normal.cn: 词干 capacitas 意为容量，也就是容纳或做事的空间。

normal.en: In law, incapacitated describes a person without legal capacity.
normal.cn: 在法律中，incapacitated 指没有法律行为能力的人。

normal.en: Insurance papers often use the phrase incapacitated from work.
normal.cn: 保险文件常用 incapacitated from work 这一说法。

normal.en: Compare incapable, which is the adjective, and incapacitate, which is the verb.
normal.cn: 对比如下两个词：incapable 是形容词，incapacitate 是动词。

normal.en: The verb usually takes a person or a machine as its object.
normal.cn: 这个动词的宾语通常是人或机器。

abstract.en: Picture a plug pulled out of the wall and a screen going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象插头被拔离墙面，屏幕一下子黑掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a chess board where every square is closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棋盘，每个格子都被封死。

abstract.en: Think of a door whose key has been taken away.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，钥匙被人收走了。

examples.en: A bad back had incapacitated her for weeks.
examples.cn: 背痛使她好几周都无法行动。

examples.en: The explosion incapacitated the vehicle and its crew.
examples.cn: 爆炸使这辆车及车上人员失去了运作能力。

examples.en: Doctors tested the drug to see how quickly it would incapacitate the muscles.
examples.cn: 医生测试了这种药，想看看它多快能让肌肉失去活动能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因卡帕西台」——人被「卡」住、帕子一盖就抬不动了，能力全无；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓取、容纳）→ capax（能容纳的）→ capacitas（容量、能力）→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 incapacitate，核心义「使失去容纳与行动的能力」。

sensesIntro.en: Incapacitate starts with a general loss of the power to act, then narrows to disabling injury, legal unfitness, and blocked function.
sensesIntro.cn: incapacitate 先指笼统地失去行动能力，再收窄为致残的伤害、法律上的无资格与机能的停摆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut wire that leaves a machine frozen mid-action.
core.cn: 核心意象：被剪断的导线，让机器僵在半路。

branches.en: The plain sense is loss of the power to act.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项是失去行动的能力。

branches.en: Physical injury and stopped function turn the ability into a body fact.
branches.cn: 身体受伤与机能停止，把「能力」变成身体上的事实。

branches.en: Legal incapacity is the formal face of the same missing capacity.
branches.cn: 法律上的无资格，是同一种能力缺失的正式面孔。

branches.en: Losing fitness for a role and losing effect both reduce capacity to nearly zero.
branches.cn: 失去胜任资格与失去效力，都把能力降到几乎为零。

branches.en: A blocked game and a disabled state are two ends of the same loss.
branches.cn: 被封锁的棋局与伤残状态，是同一次失去的两端。

intro.en: The word joins the negative prefix in- to the capacity root cap-, and from it come incapable and incapacity.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀 in- 与表示「容量」的词根 cap- 结合而成，incapable 与 incapacity 也由此而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere means to seize or hold, and capacitas means the room to hold.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为抓取、容纳，capacitas 意为容纳的空间。

items.example: The prefix in- turns capacity into incapacity.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 capacity 变成 incapacity。

items.example: Capere gives the image of holding.
items.exampleCN: capere 提供「容纳」的意象。

items.example: Capax is the direct base of the word.
items.exampleCN: capax 是这个词的直接基础。

items.example: Capacitas gives English capacity.
items.exampleCN: capacitas 演变为英语 capacity。

items.example: Capacity is the key noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: capacity 是这个词族的核心名词。

items.example: The suffix -ate makes the verb from the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把名词词干变成动词。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms incapacitation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 incapacitation。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms incapacity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 incapacity。

items.example: Incapability is the rare noun of the negative stem.
items.exampleCN: incapability 是否定词干的罕见名词形式。

items.example: Incapable keeps the negative stem.
items.exampleCN: incapable 保留否定词干。

definition_zh: 纵火者；燃烧弹；煽动性的；引起燃烧的
definition_en: designed to start a fire, or likely to stir up conflict
core_image: 一只正在燃烧的火把，被随意丢向干草堆
scene: 第 一 个义项：纵火者。老城区的木屋接连起火，警方怀疑有人故意放火。Police believe an incendiary set the empty houses alight one after another.
sceneCN: 这里 incendiary 是「纵火者」（第 1 个义项：故意放火的人）；句意：警方认为是一名纵火者把一栋栋空屋接连点着了。

pos.zh: 纵火者；燃烧弹
引起燃烧的
煽动性的；挑动的

derivatives.zh: 由词干加名词词尾「-ism」构成，义为「纵火行为；放火罪」
复数形式，义为「燃烧弹；纵火者」，常见于战事报道
罕见同族名词，义为「纵火者」

senses.title: A person who starts fires
senses.definition: a person who deliberately sets fire to property
senses.definitionCN: 蓄意放火烧毁财物的人
senses.example: The police are looking for the incendiary who burned the school.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在寻找烧毁学校的纵火者。
senses.why: The Latin verb incendere means to set on fire, and a person who does it is the first and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 incendere 意为点火燃烧，放火的人就是最直接、最字面的义项。

senses.title: A fire bomb
senses.definition: a bomb or device filled with material that bursts into flame
senses.definitionCN: 装填易燃物、落地即燃烧的炸弹或装置
senses.example: The plane dropped incendiaries on the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机向森林投下了燃烧弹。
senses.why: From the fire-setter, the word moves to the thing that carries and spreads the fire.
senses.whyCN: 从放火的人，这个词转向承载并扩散火焰的物件。

senses.title: Words that start a conflict
senses.definition: designed to make people angry or to start trouble and conflict
senses.definitionCN: 旨在激怒他人、引发争端与冲突的
senses.example: He was criticised for making incendiary remarks about the group.
senses.exampleCN: 他因对该群体发表煽动性言论而受到批评。
senses.why: If an idea can set a crowd alight, then a remark that does the same is metaphorically incendiary.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个念头能点燃一群人，那么同样能点燃情绪的言论在隐喻上就是 incendiary。

senses.title: A thing that burns on purpose
senses.definition: material or equipment that starts or spreads a fire
senses.definitionCN: 能够引发或传播火焰的材料或器材
senses.example: The chemical is an incendiary and must be stored carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化学品会引起燃烧，必须小心存放。
senses.why: As an adjective the word plainly describes the burning property of an object.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词朴素地描述某一物品燃烧的性质。

senses.title: A protest or attack by arson
senses.definition: an act of burning property as a form of attack or protest
senses.definitionCN: 以焚烧财物作为攻击或抗议手段的行为
senses.example: The unrest included several incendiaries against the port.
senses.exampleCN: 骚乱期间发生了数起针对港口的纵火袭击。
senses.why: The noun can also stand for the act itself, the strike that carries the fire.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可以指行为本身，即携带着火焰的那一次袭击。

senses.title: Heat that seems to burn the skin
senses.definition: hot or burning in effect, as if setting the body on fire
senses.definitionCN: 热得发烫、仿佛让人身体着火
senses.example: The high sun gave the sand an incendiary glare.
senses.exampleCN: 高悬的太阳让沙地泛着灼热的白光。
senses.why: Even light and weather can be described with the fire word when they burn the eyes or skin.
senses.whyCN: 当阳光与天气灼伤眼睛或皮肤时，也可以借用这个「火」的词来形容。

senses.title: A crowd-moving style
senses.definition: a style of speaking or writing that stirs people into action
senses.definitionCN: 能鼓动人们起来行动的说话或写作风格
senses.example: Her incendiary style filled the hall with energy.
senses.exampleCN: 她点燃情绪的风格让整个礼堂充满能量。
senses.why: The same metaphor of lighting a fire supports praise as well as blame when the effect is strong.
senses.whyCN: 同样一个「点火」的隐喻，在效果强烈时既能用于批评，也能用于称赞。

senses.title: A fire starter in old style
senses.definition: an old use for a thing used to light fires, such as a fireball
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指用来点火的器具，如燃烧球
senses.example: Museum texts still call this old fireball an incendiary.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的文字仍把这枚旧式燃烧球称作 incendiary。
senses.why: Historical writings use the word for any object whose job is to carry flame from one place to another.
senses.whyCN: 历史文本用这个词指任何负责把火焰带到另一个地方的东西。

intro.en: Incendiary comes from Latin incendere, to set on fire, through the noun incendium, a fire or blaze.
intro.cn: incendiary 来自拉丁语动词 incendere（点着火），经由名词 incendium（火灾、烈焰）演变成形。

items.en: Candere means to shine or glow, a root shared with candle.
items.cn: candere 意为发光、泛白热，与英语 candle 同源。

items.en: In- adds into, giving incendere, to set on fire.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「进入」，构成 incendere，意为点着、放火。

items.en: Incendium means a fire, while incendiarius means a fire-setter.
items.cn: incendium 意为火灾，incendiarius 意为放火者。

items.en: Incendary enters English as a noun for a fire-raiser.
items.cn: incendary 作为「放火者」的名词进入英语。

items.en: The spelling settles as incendiary and the adjective sense appears.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 incendiary，形容词义项随之出现。

items.en: Modern English uses the adjective mainly for stirring or dangerous language.
items.cn: 现代英语多把形容词用于煽动性或危险的言辞。

note.en: Incendiary shares the Latin burning root with incendiarism and sits near words about fire, arson, and stirring trouble.
note.cn: incendiary 与 incendiarism 共享表示「燃烧」的拉丁词根，并与纵火、起火及煽动事端的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: a substance burned for its sweet smell
entries.definitionCN: 同源，本指把香料点火焚出香气，名词义为「香」

entries.definition: serving to stir up or provoke
entries.definitionCN: 同族冷僻形容词，义为「挑动情绪的」

entries.definition: something that encourages an action
entries.definitionCN: 拼写与发音相近，但义为「激励；动机」，与火无关

entries.definition: easy to catch fire
designed to make people angry
the crime of setting property on fire

normalIntro.en: Incendiary keeps the Latin picture of setting a fire, and English stretched that fire into words and conflicts.
normalIntro.cn: incendiary 保留了拉丁语「点火」的画面，英语又把这把火延伸到了言辞与冲突上。

normal.en: The glow root candere also gives English candle, a small steady light.
normal.cn: 表示发光的词根「candere」也构成英语 candle，即一支安静的小火苗。

normal.en: Incendiary keeps the Latin stem incendi-, shared by incendiarism.
normal.cn: incendiary 保留拉丁词干「incendi-」，incendiarism 也出于同一词干。

normal.en: Journalists often pair the adjective with remarks, rhetoric, and speech.
normal.cn: 记者常把这个形容词与言论、说辞、演讲搭配使用。

normal.en: In science writing incendiary means simply that a material burns.
normal.cn: 在科学写作中，这个词只表示材料会燃烧。

normal.en: The people who deal with these fires are called incendiaries as a noun.
normal.cn: 作名词时，这个词的复数形「incendiaries」指纵火者或燃烧弹。

abstract.en: Picture a torch thrown onto dry straw at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一支火把被扔进干草堆。

abstract.en: Imagine a lecture hall where a single sentence sets the room alight.
abstract.cn: 想象一间演讲厅，只用一句话就让全场沸腾。

abstract.en: Think of a burning football knocking down lit matches.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚燃烧着的火球滚过去，一路点燃火柴。

examples.en: The fire brigade searched for the incendiary in the ruins.
examples.cn: 消防队员在废墟中搜寻那名纵火者。

examples.en: Officials warned that incendiary language could spark fresh violence.
examples.cn: 官员警告说，煽动性的言辞可能引发新的暴力。

examples.en: Incendiaries damaged three buses in the depot that night.
examples.cn: 那天晚上，燃烧装置损坏了车场里的三辆公交车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「In森迪尔」——森迪尔一进森林就点火，放火的人也叫 incendiary；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 candere（发白热、发光）+ 前缀 in-（进入）→ incendere（点火焚烧）→ incendium（火灾）→ 英语 incendiary，核心义「把火点起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Incendiary starts with the person who sets the fire, then the bomb, and finally spreads to words and heat that catch fire figuratively.
sensesIntro.cn: incendiary 先从放火的人开始，再到燃烧弹，最后延伸到同样会「着火」的言辞与灼热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torch dropped onto a pile of dry straw.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支火把被丢进干草堆。

branches.en: The fire-setter is the oldest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 放火者是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: The bomb and the attack are the weapon-shaped forms of the same fire.
branches.cn: 燃烧弹与纵火袭击，是同一把火在武器形态上的化形。

branches.en: Words that stir people borrow the flicker of the same fire.
branches.cn: 鼓动人心的言辞借用了同一簇火焰的闪动。

branches.en: Materials and old starting objects keep the plain burning sense.
branches.cn: 材料与旧式点火物保留了最朴素的燃烧义项。

branches.en: Heat that burns the skin closes the circle back to literal fire.
branches.cn: 灼烧皮肤的炙热把圈子绕回了字面上的火。

intro.en: The word is built on Latin incendere, to set on fire, from in- plus candere, to glow, the root of candle.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语 incendere（点火）之上，由在前缀 in- 与表示发光的 candere 构成，candle 也出自这一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin candere means to glow, and incendiarius means the person who sets fires.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 candere 意为发光，incendiarius 意为放火的人。

items.example: The prefix in- links glow with setting fire.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把发光与点火连接起来。

items.example: Candere gives the glow at the heart of fire.
items.exampleCN: candere 提供火星子般的灼白之色。

items.example: Candela is the light beside the fire word.
items.exampleCN: candela 是火字旁边的那束光。

items.example: Incendere is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: incendere 是直接的动词来源。

items.example: Incendium names the blaze itself.
items.exampleCN: incendium 指烈焰本身。

items.example: Incendiarius is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: incendiarius 是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms the English adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成英语的形容词与名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms incendiarism, the practice of arson.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 incendiarism，指纵火行为。

items.example: Incendiarism names the crime of the arsonist.
items.exampleCN: incendiarism 指纵火犯所犯的罪行。

items.example: Incendiary stretches from fire to burning words.
items.exampleCN: incendiary 从火焰延伸到了灼人的言辞。

definition_zh: （名词）香；熏香；（动词）使发怒；激怒
definition_en: a substance that burns with a sweet smell, or, as a verb, to make someone very angry
core_image: 细烟从香柱顶端的红点里一缕缕上升，飘满整间屋子
scene: 寺院铜炉里点着一炷香，烟丝慢慢升到屋顶，再顺着门缝飘进庭院。A thin thread of incense smoke curled up from the bronze burner and drifted across the courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里 incense 是「香、熏香」（第 1 个义项：点燃后散发香气的物质）；句意：一缕细细的香烟从铜炉里盘上升起，飘过庭院。这个义项最贴近「香烟从红点里升起」的核心画面。

pos.zh: 香；熏香；香气
使发怒；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由动词加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「焚香；（宗教礼仪中的）奉香」
由拉丁词干 incens- 加后缀 -ory 构成，指「香炉；奉香容器」
由过去分词形容词化而来，义为「怒不可遏的」

senses.title: A sweet-smelling substance
senses.definition: a substance, often a resin, gum, or stick, that is burned to give off a pleasant smell
senses.definitionCN: 常为树脂、香料或香柱，点燃后散发好闻气味的物质
senses.example: The temple was heavy with the smoke of burning incense.
senses.exampleCN: 庙里弥漫着浓浓的香烟味。
senses.why: Latin incendere means to set on fire, and incense is the stuff you set burning for its smell, so the word names a fuel of fragrance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 incendere 意为「点燃」，incense 正是为了香气而被点燃的东西，所以这个词直接指向「被点着的香料」。

senses.title: The fragrant smoke or scent
senses.definition: the fragrant smoke or perfume that such a substance gives off
senses.definitionCN: 香燃烧时散出的香气与烟雾
senses.example: A faint incense of sandalwood clung to her clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的衣服上留着一丝檀香的香气。
senses.why: Because the smell is the whole point of burning it, the word slides from the fuel itself to the perfume that fills the air.
senses.whyCN: 点香的意义就在那股香味，于是这个词从「香料本身」自然滑向「弥漫在空中的香气」。

senses.title: To make someone very angry
senses.definition: to make someone extremely angry, usually on purpose or by unfair behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 使人极度愤怒，常指有意为之或由于不公之举
senses.example: The unfair decision incensed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 这个不公的决定激怒了整个团队。
senses.why: This is a different word from the same Latin verb incendere, to set fire: to incense someone is to set their temper ablaze.
senses.whyCN: 这是同出拉丁语 incendere（点火）的另一个词：把某人的怒气「点着」，就是激怒他，和点香共用「点火」的画面。

senses.title: Ritual use in temples and churches
senses.definition: the practice of burning fragrant substances as part of worship or remembrance
senses.definitionCN: 在礼拜或纪念活动中焚香的做法
senses.example: Incense has been offered at Buddhist shrines for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 佛教圣地焚香的习俗已延续数百年。
senses.why: Smoke rises, so the ceremony makes it an offering that carries prayers upward, giving the noun a fixed place in ritual.
senses.whyCN: 烟气向上飘升，仪式便把焚香当作把祈愿送上天的奉献，于是名词在宗教礼仪中固定下来。

senses.title: Flattery meant to please
senses.definition: praise or flattery offered to someone for the sake of pleasing them
senses.definitionCN: 为讨好而说的赞美或奉承话
senses.example: He incensed the judge with smooth words and a low bow.
senses.exampleCN: 他用顺耳的恭维和深深一躬讨好那位评判。
senses.why: Sweet-smelling smoke is offered to honour a deity, and the same image moves to symbolise sweet words offered to win favour.
senses.whyCN: 香烟是被献给神灵以示尊崇的礼物，这幅画面被借来比喻「用甜言蜜语讨好别人」，于是有了恭维义。

intro.en: Incense comes from Latin incensum, something burned, and its history is tangled with a second, unrelated word about anger that happens to share the same spelling.
intro.cn: incense 来自拉丁语 incensum（被烧的东西）；它的历史还与另一个拼写相同、意义却无关的「发怒」词纠缠在一起。

items.en: Incendere means to set on fire, built on the verb root for kindling.
items.cn: 拉丁语 incendere 意为「点燃」，由表示「引火」的动词词根构成。

items.en: The participle incensum means something burnt, and in use it names the fragrant stuff offered in smoke.
items.cn: 分词 incensum 意为「被烧的东西」，实际使用中指以烟供奉的香料。

items.en: The form encens carries the burning smell into French.
items.cn: 法语形 encens 把这个「燃烧的香气」带进法语。

items.en: Encens enters English as a noun for the substance burned in churches.
items.cn: 中世纪英语中 encens 进入英语，指教堂里焚烧的香料。

items.en: A separate verb incensare, to provoke, also from incendere, develops the meaning of rousing anger.
items.cn: 另有一个拉丁动词 incensare（挑动），同样出自 incendere，发展出「激起怒火」之义。

items.en: The two words settle into one spelling, giving English a noun for perfume and a verb for fury.
items.cn: 两个词最终落在同一拼写上，英语因此同时得到「香料」名词和「激怒」动词。

note.en: Incense sits between other words of the same Latin fire root and between everyday words for scent and for anger.
note.cn: incense 处在一组同出拉丁语「火」根的词之间，也处在表示「香气」与表示「愤怒」的日常词之间。

entries.definition: a container in which incense is burned during a ceremony
entries.definitionCN: 仪式中焚烧香料的香炉（同源名词）

entries.definition: designed to start a fire, or tending to stir up trouble
entries.definitionCN: 纵火的；（言论）煽动性的（同源形容词）

entries.definition: very great or extreme in strength
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的；剧烈的（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自「拉紧」的词根）

entries.definition: a sweet smell, or a liquid worn for its scent
a pleasant, often lasting smell
to make someone extremely angry

normalIntro.en: Link incense to the Latin fire verb incendere and notice how one spelling serves two jobs, a smell and a temper.
normalIntro.cn: 把 incense 与拉丁语的火动词 incendere 联系起来，并留意同一拼写承担两种任务：一种气味与一腔怒火。

normal.en: Latin incendere, to set on fire, is the root behind both meanings.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 incendere（点燃）是两个义项共用的词根。

normal.en: As a noun the stress falls early: IN-cense, the stick in the burner.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音在前：IN-cense，指香炉里那根香。

normal.en: As a verb the stress moves late: in-CENSE, to make someone furious.
normal.cn: 作动词时重音后移：in-CENSE，指激怒某人。

normal.en: The adjective incensed means angry, and it matches the verb, not the smell.
normal.cn: 形容词 incensed 表示愤怒，与动词义相配，而不是香料义。

normal.en: Compare perfume and fragrance: incense is burned, while the others are worn or sprayed.
normal.cn: 对比 perfume 与 fragrance：incense 是烧出来的，另外两个是涂抹或喷洒的。

abstract.en: See a crimson tip of an incense stick slowly eating down toward your fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象香柱顶端一点暗红慢慢往下烧，越来越靠近手指。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room robed in blue-grey smoke and the faint sweetness of sandalwood.
abstract.cn: 想象整间屋子罩在蓝灰色的烟里，飘着淡淡的檀香。

abstract.en: Imagine a face flushing red as the temper inside is lit like a taper.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸涨得通红，心里的怒火像被烛火点燃。

examples.en: She lit a stick of incense in front of the family portrait.
examples.cn: 她在全家福前点了一炷香。

examples.en: Many visitors were incensed by the sudden rise in ticket prices.
examples.cn: 门票突然涨价让许多游客十分愤怒。

examples.en: The incense burner is so old that its surface is dark with soot.
examples.cn: 那只香炉太旧了，表面被烟熏得发黑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「应身死」——心里点起一把火，气得应声倒下；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 incendere（点燃）+ 分词 incensum（被烧的东西）→ 古法语 encens → 英语 incense（香料）；另由拉丁语 incensare（挑动）→ 英语 incense（激怒），两根同出于「火」。

sensesIntro.en: Incense begins as the fragrant material you set alight, moves to the smoke and scent it releases, then to temples and offerings, then to sweet words used as a gift, and finally to a separate verb that lights a temper.
sensesIntro.cn: incense 从「被点燃的香料」开始，转到它释放的烟雾与香气，再到庙宇中的奉香，又比喻为用来讨好的甜言，最后落到一个点燃怒火的同形动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin ribbon of smoke rising from a glowing tip in a bronze burner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根发红的香头在铜炉里升出细长的烟。

branches.en: The material that burns for its smell is the everyday noun.
branches.cn: 为香味而焚烧的物质是日常使用的名词义。

branches.en: The scent released by the material is the second noun sense.
branches.cn: 香料释放出的香气是第二个名词义。

branches.en: The verb came by a different route, yet it uses the same picture of lighting a fire.
branches.cn: 动词义来自另一条路径，却沿用「点火」的同一幅画面。

branches.en: Ritual offering and flattery are both gifts offered like sweet smoke.
branches.cn: 仪式奉香与恭维讨好，都像香一样是被献出的礼物。

branches.en: Both rest on Latin incendere, to set on fire.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立在拉丁语 incendere（点燃）之上。

intro.en: Incense is a borrowed Latin word: the stem incens- from incendere carries the idea of setting alight, and English later grew words such as censer and incensed around it.
intro.cn: incense 是借自拉丁语的词：词干 incens- 来自 incendere，带着「点燃」的意思；英语后来又围绕它长出 censer、incensed 等词。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, incendere is to set on fire, incensum is what is burnt, and incensare is to provoke. English borrowed the noun and the verb separately.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中 incendere 是「点燃」，incensum 是「被烧的东西」，incensare 是「挑动」；英语分别借入了名词与动词。

items.example: The stem incens- carries the idea of burning.
items.exampleCN: 词干 incens- 承载「燃烧」的意味。

items.example: Incendere is the fire verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: incendere 是整组词背后的火动词。

items.example: Incensum supplied the noun meaning.
items.exampleCN: incensum 提供了名词义。

items.example: The adjective kept the fire image.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了火的形象。

items.meaning: past participle ending used as an adjective
items.meaningCN: 过去分词词尾，可作形容词
items.example: The suffix -ed makes incensed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 incensed。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms incensation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 incensation。

items.meaningCN: 表示场所或器具的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ory forms incensory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 incensory。

items.example: A censer swings on chains in the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 仪式中香炉在链条上摇摆。

items.example: To cense the altar is to honour it with smoke.
items.exampleCN: 给祭坛焚香就是用香烟表示敬意。

items.example: Incensing the room filled it with scent.
items.exampleCN: 焚香让整个房间弥漫香气。

definition_zh: 不断的；持续不停的（多指令人厌烦的事）
definition_en: continuing without a pause, especially in a way that is tiring or annoying
core_image: 雨点不停地敲在铁皮屋顶上，一夜到天亮都没停过
scene: 楼上的水管漏水，滴水声每隔一秒敲一下盆底，吵得人整夜睡不着。The incessant drip from the leaking pipe kept her awake all night.
sceneCN: 这里 incessant 是「持续不停的」（第 1 个义项：没有停顿地连续发生，多含厌烦意味）；句意：漏水管道持续不断的滴答声让她整夜无法入睡。这个义项最贴近「雨点不停敲屋顶」的核心画面。

pos.zh: 不断的；持续不停的；频繁的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不断地；没完没了地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ancy 构成，义为「持续不断（的状态）」
同出拉丁语 cessare（停止）的名词，义为「中止；停止」

senses.title: Continuing without a pause
senses.definition: going on and on without ever stopping, usually of something tiring or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 一直持续、从不停止，通常指令人疲惫或厌烦之事
senses.example: The incessant drumming of the rain made sleep impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水不停地敲打，让人无法入睡。
senses.why: The Latin prefix in- adds not to cessare, to stop, so the adjective literally means not stopping, a thing that never takes a break.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 表示「不」，加在 cessare（停止）之上，所以这个词的字面意思就是「不停止」，指一刻也不歇的事物。

senses.title: Too frequent to bear
senses.definition: happening so often and so relentlessly that it becomes a burden
senses.definitionCN: 发生得过于频繁、过于密集，以致成为负担
senses.example: Her incessant questions wore the teacher out by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她没完没了的问题到中午就把老师累坏了。
senses.why: The word rarely stays neutral: constant sound or repeated asking wears a person down, so frequency itself becomes the complaint.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很少是中性的口气：持续的声音或反复的追问会把人磨垮，于是「频繁」本身就成了一种抱怨。

senses.title: Continuous in natural processes
senses.definition: used of natural forces such as rain, wind, or waves that carry on without relief
senses.definitionCN: 用于雨、风、浪等自然力量连绵不断、毫无间歇的情形
senses.example: The incessant wind flattened the young corn by morning.
senses.exampleCN: 到了早晨，连绵不停的狂风把嫩玉米都吹倒了。
senses.why: Weather has no concern for the human need for rest, so the word describes nature doing what it does without a pause.
senses.whyCN: 天气不管人需不需要休息，这个词恰好描述自然界不顾一切地持续下去，所以常用来说雨、风与浪。

senses.title: Unbroken in writing about time
senses.definition: describing a period of work, effort, or change that runs on with no gap
senses.definitionCN: 形容一段工作、努力或变化毫无间隙地延续
senses.example: Years of incessant drilling finally found oil.
senses.exampleCN: 经过多年不间断的钻探，他们终于找到了石油。
senses.why: In formal writing the word drops the nagging tone and simply marks effort that refuses to stop.
senses.whyCN: 在正式文本里，这个词褪去「唠叨」的口气，只标明一种拒绝停下的努力。

senses.title: In speech, of a talker
senses.definition: used of a person who talks or acts without any let-up
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人说话或做事一刻不停
senses.example: His incessant chatter drove the whole office to distraction.
senses.exampleCN: 他喋喋不休的闲谈让整个办公室都无法专心。
senses.why: The prefix in- again denies a pause, so a talker who never lets up can be called incessant like a sound.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 又一次否定了停顿，于是从不停口的人也能像声音一样被形容为「incessant」。

intro.en: Incessant is built in Latin from in-, not, and cessans, the present participle of cessare, to stop or cease, and it came into English through French.
intro.cn: incessant 是在拉丁语中构成的：in-（不）+ cessans（cessare 的现在分词，意为「停止」），再经法语进入英语。

items.en: Cessare means to stop, to be idle, or to linger, a frequentative form of cedere, to go.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cessare 意为「停止、闲下来、拖延」，是 cedere（走）的反复形式。

items.en: The participle cessans means one who stops, so in-cessans means one who does not stop.
items.cn: 分词 cessans 意为「停止着的」，所以 in-cessans 就是「不停歇的」。

items.en: Christian writers use incessans for prayer and praise that carry on without ceasing.
items.cn: 公元四至六世纪的教父著作里，incessans 用来形容不停地祷告与赞颂。

items.en: French adopts the Latin word as incessant, keeping the plain sense of unending.
items.cn: 法语把这词借为 incessant，保留「不停止」的原义。

items.en: English takes the word from French and slowly applies it to noises, complaints, and effort.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入该词，逐渐把它用到噪音、抱怨与努力之上。

items.en: The word settles into a slightly negative tone, of things that go on too long.
items.cn: 此后这个词定型为略带贬义，多指持续得过久的事物。

note.en: Incessant belongs to the family of words built on Latin cessare, to stop, and it stands close to everyday words for constant and uninterrupted that lack its nagging tone.
note.cn: incessant 属于以拉丁语 cessare（停止）为基础的一族词，它靠近表示「不断的」日常词，但比它们多了几分令人厌烦的口气。

entries.definition: the stopping of something, especially for a period
to stop doing or happening
the beginning of an organisation or activity
entries.definitionCN: 开端；创始（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自「抓起」一义）

entries.definition: staying the same or happening all the time
happening without a break or gap
seeming to have no end and going on too long

normalIntro.en: Keep incessant anchored to Latin cessare, to stop, hidden inside the English verb cease, and remember the prefix denies it.
normalIntro.cn: 把 incessant 固定在拉丁语 cessare（停止）上，这个成分也藏在英语动词 cease 里；再记住前缀 in- 把它否定掉。

normal.en: Split the word as in-cess-ant, where cess comes from Latin cessare, to stop.
normal.cn: 把这个词拆成 in-cess-ant：其中 cess 来自拉丁语 cessare，意为停止。

normal.en: The same root appears in cease and cessation, both about stopping.
normal.cn: 同一个词根出现在 cease 与 cessation 里，两者都与「停止」有关。

normal.en: The prefix in- negates it, so in-cess-ant means simply not stopping.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 起否定作用，所以 in-cess-ant 就是「不停止」。

normal.en: The adverb incessantly is the usual form in speech: it rained incessantly.
normal.cn: 口语里更常用副词 incessantly，比如「雨下个不停」。

normal.en: Compare continuous: continuous is neutral, while incessant carries a tone of complaint.
normal.cn: 对比 continuous：continuous 是中性的，incessant 则带抱怨的口气。

abstract.en: Hear a drumbeat that never lets up, one tap after another with no silence in between.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵永不停歇的鼓点，一下接一下，中间没有片刻安静。

abstract.en: Picture a small question mark popping up every few seconds, all day long.
abstract.cn: 想象每隔几秒就冒出一个问号，一整天一个接一个。

abstract.en: Watch clouds rolling across the sky with no gap opening between them.
abstract.cn: 想象云层在天空翻滚，彼此之间始终不露缝隙。

examples.en: The incessant noise from the building site gave her a headache.
examples.cn: 工地上不停的噪音让她头疼。

examples.en: After three days of incessant rain, the river began to flood.
examples.cn: 连下三天不停的雨之后，河水开始上涨。

examples.en: The child asked questions incessantly until bedtime.
examples.cn: 那个孩子一直问个不停，直到睡觉时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「应塞身特」——雨点一直往里塞，把全身都塞得湿透，一刻也不停；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ cessare（停止，其分词为 cessans）→ 晚期拉丁语 incessans → 法语 incessant → 英语 incessant，核心义「一点也停不下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Incessant starts from the plain denial of stopping, turns negative once it describes things that wear people down, then settles into descriptions of weather, long effort, and talkative people.
sensesIntro.cn: incessant 从字面上「不停止」出发，一用来形容耗人的事物便带上负面色彩，随后固定用在天气、长期努力与喋喋不休的人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: raindrops drumming on a tin roof without a single silent second.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨点不停敲打铁皮屋顶，没有一秒安静。

branches.en: The plain sense of never pausing is the everyday core.
branches.cn: 字面上的「从不停顿」是日常核心义。

branches.en: Repetition that wears a person down adds the tone of complaint.
branches.cn: 过度重复把人磨垮，于是添上了抱怨的口气。

branches.en: Rain, wind, and waves never rest, so the word suits them naturally.
branches.cn: 雨、风与浪从不停息，这个词自然用得来。

branches.en: Formal writing uses it for long effort with no gaps.
branches.cn: 正式写作里用它描述毫无间隙的长期努力。

branches.en: A talkative person is the human version of ceaseless noise.
branches.cn: 喋喋不休的人，就是无休止噪音的人格化版本。

intro.en: Incessant is made of an English-looking prefix and suffix around the Latin root cess-, and the wider family includes cease, cessation, and incessantly.
intro.cn: incessant 由类似英语的前缀与后缀包住拉丁词根 cess-，同族的还有 cease、cessation 与 incessantly。

latinIntro.en: Latin cessare, to cease, gave the root; in- denies it; and the participles cessans and cessatum are the shapes English saw.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自拉丁语 cessare（停止），in- 表示否定，英语接触到的形态则是分词 cessans 与 cessatum。

items.example: The prefix in- denies what follows.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定后面的部分。

items.example: The root cess- carries the idea of stopping.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cess- 承载「停止」的意思。

items.example: Cessare is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: cessare 是基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ant makes an adjective from a participle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 把分词变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms incessantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 incessantly。

items.example: The suffix -ancy forms incessancy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ancy 构成 incessancy。

items.example: Cease is the plain English verb.
items.exampleCN: cease 是朴素的英语动词。

items.example: Cessation keeps the stopping sense as a noun.
items.exampleCN: cessation 以名词形式保留「停止」之义。

items.meaning: the view that certain gifts ceased
items.meaningCN: 终止论（某些恩赐已停止的观点）
items.example: The suffix -ism turns it into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 把它变成一种学说名称。

items.meaning: the point at which a legal right ends
items.example: Cesser is a law term for the end of a right.
items.exampleCN: cesser 是法律术语，指权利终止的时刻。

definition_zh: 焚化；把……烧成灰；烧毁
definition_en: to burn something completely, usually waste, until nothing but ash is left
core_image: 垃圾在炉膛里烧成亮红，最后只剩一层灰白的粉末
scene: 医院把用过的绷带和针管送进高温焚烧炉，炉火把整袋东西烧到只剩灰色粉末。The hospital incinerates used medical waste at a very high temperature.
sceneCN: 这里 incinerate 是「焚化、烧成灰」（第 1 个义项：把物体彻底烧尽，只剩灰烬）；句意：医院用很高的温度焚化使用过的医疗废物。这个义项最贴近「垃圾在炉膛里烧成灰」的核心画面。

pos.zh: 焚化；把……烧成灰；烧毁
被烧成灰；焚毁

derivatives.zh: 由动词加后缀 -ation 构成，义为「焚化；烧成灰的处理方式」
由动词加施动后缀 -ator 构成，义为「焚烧炉；焚化炉」
由动词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可焚化的」

senses.title: To burn something to ash
senses.definition: to burn something completely, usually waste, at a high temperature until only ash remains
senses.definitionCN: 在高温下把某物（通常为废物）彻底烧尽，只留下灰烬
senses.example: The hospital incinerates used bandages at a very high temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 医院在极高的温度下焚化用过的绷带。
senses.why: Latin cinis means ashes, and the verb names the moment when even the ashes of a fire are reached, so the object is destroyed down to its residue.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cinis 意为「灰」，这个动词正指烧到只剩灰的那一步，因此宾语是被彻底毁掉、化为残渣的。

senses.title: To destroy by fire
senses.definition: to destroy a building, document, or other object with fire
senses.definitionCN: 用火毁掉房屋、文件或其他物体
senses.example: The old records were incinerated in the courtyard fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案在院子里的火堆中被烧成了灰。
senses.why: If the verb means burning until only ash is left, then burning anything out of existence, from a letter to a whole building, falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词的意思是「烧到只剩灰」，那么把书信、甚至整座房子烧得不存在，也自然落在它的范围内。

senses.title: To catch fire and burn away
senses.definition: of an object, to burn up by itself, especially in a fire or furnace
senses.definitionCN: 物体自身在火灾或炉中被烧尽
senses.example: The dry timber incinerated in minutes once the shed caught fire.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子一着火，干燥的木料几分钟内就烧成了灰。
senses.why: The same event can be told from the object side, so the verb also works without an object in English.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事也可以从物体的角度来叙述，所以这个词在英语里也能不带宾语，表示「被烧掉」。

senses.title: In waste and energy plants
senses.definition: the industrial burning of waste to reduce its bulk and recover heat
senses.definitionCN: 工业上将垃圾焚烧以减小体积并回收热量
senses.example: Large cities now incinerate most of their household rubbish.
senses.exampleCN: 大城市如今焚化掉大部分生活垃圾。
senses.why: Modern waste plants put the fire in a sealed furnace, so the old burning word becomes the technical term for controlled disposal.
senses.whyCN: 现代垃圾厂把火关进密封炉膛，这个古老的「烧」字就成了表示受控处置的技术用语。

senses.title: Of bodies after death
senses.definition: to reduce a body to ash by fire as part of a funeral
senses.definitionCN: 丧葬过程中用火把遗体化为骨灰
senses.example: The body was incinerated and the ashes buried under the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 遗体被火化，骨灰埋在了树下。
senses.why: Funeral houses use the same Latin word as waste plants, because the process, fire turning a body to ash, is the same.
senses.whyCN: 殡仪馆和垃圾厂用的是同一个拉丁语词，因为过程相同——用火把身体化为灰。

intro.en: Incinerate is built on Latin cinis, cineris, ash, with the prefix in- marking the movement into ash; English took the word through Latin incinerare and French.
intro.cn: incinerate 以拉丁语 cinis、属格 cineris（灰）为基础，前缀 in- 标示「进入灰烬」；英语经拉丁语 incinerare 与法语借入。

items.en: Cinis means ash, and its genitive cineris gives the fuller stem seen in the compound.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cinis 意为「灰」，其属格 cineris 提供了复合词里更完整的词干。

items.en: The adjective cinerosus means full of ash or ashy.
items.cn: 形容词 cinerosus 意为「多灰的、灰烬般的」。

items.en: The verb incinerare means to burn to ashes.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语动词 incinerare 意为「烧成灰」。

items.en: French borrows the learned word as incinérer, used in writing about funeral fires.
items.cn: 法语在十六世纪借入这个书面词，写作 incinérer，用于描述火葬。

items.en: English adopts incinerate in learned prose, first about burial rites and later about burning any matter.
items.cn: 英语在书面散文里采用 incinerate，起初讲殡葬仪式，后来扩展到烧毁任何物质。

items.en: Town burning plants give English the noun incinerator, which fixes the verb to waste disposal.
items.cn: 城市焚烧厂带来了名词 incinerator，把这个动词固定到垃圾处理领域。

note.en: Incinerate belongs with other fire verbs but is the one that insists on ash; its look-alikes share the ashen root or merely the spelling.
note.cn: incinerate 属于一组「火」动词，但它特别强调「烧成灰」；它的形近词要么同根，要么只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: a furnace or machine for burning waste
entries.definitionCN: 焚烧炉；垃圾焚化设备（同根派生名词）

entries.definition: a piece of partly burnt coal or wood
entries.definitionCN: 煤渣；余烬（同出「灰」的词根）

entries.definition: to hint at something unpleasantly without saying it directly
entries.definitionCN: 暗示；含沙射影（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to be on fire, or to destroy with fire
to burn a dead body to ashes
to bring something to a certain state, as to ash
entries.definitionCN: 使……变成（可与「烧成灰」连用）

normalIntro.en: Keep incinerate tied to Latin cinis and cineris, ash, a root that also shows in the English word cinder.
normalIntro.cn: 把 incinerate 系在拉丁语 cinis、属格 cineris（灰）上，这个词根在英语 cinder 里也能看到。

normal.en: Latin cinis, ash, sits inside incinerate, with cineris as its fuller stem.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cinis（灰）藏在 incinerate 里，更完整的词干是 cineris。

normal.en: The English word cinder, a partly burnt lump, comes from the same ashen root.
normal.cn: 英语 cinder 指烧了一半的块状物，也出自同一个「灰」词根。

normal.en: The -ate ending shows a borrowed Latin verb, so the object is the thing turned to ash.
normal.cn: -ate 词尾表明这是借来的拉丁语动词，宾语即是化为灰的东西。

normal.en: The place where it happens is the incinerator, and the process is incineration.
normal.cn: 发生这件事的地方是 incinerator，整个过程叫 incineration。

normal.en: Compare burn and cremate: incinerate is the technical word, often for waste.
normal.cn: 对比 burn 与 cremate：incinerate 是技术性用语，常专门用于废物。

abstract.en: See a paper bag drop into a furnace and come out as a thin grey film.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸袋掉进炉子，出来时只剩薄薄一层灰。

abstract.en: Picture the hall of a waste plant where rubbish slides into a mouth of fire.
abstract.cn: 想象垃圾处理厂的大厅，垃圾一路滑进一张火口。

abstract.en: Hold a pinch of ash and imagine the whole object it once was inside it.
abstract.cn: 捏起一小撮灰，想象它曾经是完整的一件物品。

examples.en: The plant incinerates medical waste at over a thousand degrees.
examples.cn: 这家工厂在千度以上的高温中焚化医疗废物。

examples.en: Critics warn that incinerating rubbish releases toxic fumes.
examples.cn: 批评者警告说，焚烧垃圾会释放有毒气体。

examples.en: The letters were incinerated to keep the secret safe.
examples.cn: 为了保守秘密，那些信件被烧成了灰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因心内锐」——心里一急，火气锐利地往上冲，把东西烧成灰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 cinis / cineris（灰）+ 动词词尾 → 晚期拉丁语 incinerare（烧成灰）→ 法语 incinérer → 英语 incinerate，核心义「烧到只剩灰」。

sensesIntro.en: Incinerate begins with the image of burning something wholly to ash, widens to destroying anything by fire, and gathers its sharpest uses in waste plants and funeral rites.
sensesIntro.cn: incinerate 从「把某物彻底烧成灰」的画面出发，扩展为「用火烧毁任何东西」，最鲜明的用法则集中在垃圾处理与丧葬上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: refuse glowing red in a furnace and settling into pale grey ash.
core.cn: 核心意象：垃圾在炉膛里烧得通红，最后落成灰白的粉末。

branches.en: The sense of burning down to ash is the technical core.
branches.cn: 「烧到只剩灰」是技术核心义。

branches.en: Destroying something with fire is the same process with a visible result.
branches.cn: 用火烧毁某物，就是同一过程留下显见的结果。

branches.en: The destroyer can be ignored, and the object alone burns away.
branches.cn: 可以略去施动者，只看物体自己烧尽。

branches.en: Waste plants and funeral houses both put the fire in a sealed furnace.
branches.cn: 垃圾厂与殡仪馆都把火关在密闭炉膛里。

branches.en: All three end in ash, whether the object burns for industry or for ritual.
branches.cn: 无论出于工业还是仪式，三者最后都归于灰烬。

intro.en: Incinerate is a Latin-derived compound: the prefix in-, the ashen root ciner-, and the verb ending; the family includes incineration, incinerator, and the related word cinder.
intro.cn: incinerate 是拉丁语来源的复合词：前缀 in-、表示「灰」的词根 ciner- 与动词词尾；同族有 incineration、incinerator 以及相关的 cinder。

latinIntro.en: Latin cinis, genitive cineris, is ash; the adjective cinerosus is ashy; and incinerare is to burn to ashes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cinis（属格 cineris）是「灰」，形容词 cinerosus 是「灰似的」，动词 incinerare 是「烧成灰」。

items.example: The prefix in- points towards a result.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 指向一个结果状态。

items.example: The root ciner- carries the idea of ash.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ciner- 承载「灰」的意思。

items.example: Cinis is the noun at the centre.
items.exampleCN: cinis 是居于中心的名词。

items.example: The ending -ate marks a borrowed Latinate verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标示借来的拉丁式动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms incineration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 incineration。

items.meaning: the agent or device that does
items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或器具的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ator forms incinerator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ator 构成 incinerator。

items.example: The suffix -able forms incinerable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 incinerable。

items.meaning: a partly burned piece of fuel
items.example: Cinder shares the ashen root.
items.exampleCN: cinder 共享「灰」的词根。

items.meaning: of ashes, as a urn for them
items.example: Cinerary urns hold the ashes.
items.exampleCN: cinerary 指盛放骨灰的罐子。

items.example: The prefix re- gives reincinerate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 构成 reincinerate。

definition_zh: 煽动；鼓动；激起（敌意或强烈反应）
definition_en: to encourage or stir someone into doing something lawless or violent, or to stir up a strong feeling or reaction
core_image: 有人往将熄的炭堆里再添一把干柴，火苗猛地窜起
scene: 广场上人群开始骚动，一个年轻人跳上箱子挥着手大喊。A loud speaker tried to incite the crowd to attack the police station.
sceneCN: 这里 incite 是「煽动别人去做违法或暴力的事」（第 1 个义项：鼓动他人采取激烈或非法的行动）；句意：一个高声的叫喊者试图煽动人群攻击警察局。画面里有箱子、举起的拳头和攒动的人头。

pos.zh: 煽动；鼓动；激起：指推动他人去做违法、暴力或激烈的行为

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀构成，义为「煽动；挑唆；煽动性的行为」，法律上指煽动罪
动词加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「鼓动者；煽动者」
现在分词作形容词，义为「煽动性的；挑唆的」，如煽动性言论
与本词共用拉丁动词，义为「引用；传唤」，本词即在其前加 in- 前缀构成

senses.title: To stir people into unlawful or violent action
senses.titleCN: 煽动；鼓动他人做违法或暴力的事
senses.definition: to urge or stir other people to do something that is illegal, violent or disruptive
senses.definitionCN: 鼓动、激使别人去做违法、暴力或破坏性的事情
senses.example: The leaflets were designed to incite the miners to strike illegally.
senses.exampleCN: 这些传单意在煽动矿工非法罢工。
senses.why: The in- prefix makes something move quickly, and citare is to set in motion; incite is putting other people into motion.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「使……动起来」，citare 意为催动；被催动起来的要是别人，于是这个义项就落到了「把人推向行动」上，带有违法或暴力的色彩。

senses.title: To provoke a strong feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling, such as anger, hatred or curiosity, to arise in people
senses.definitionCN: 使人们心中产生愤怒、仇恨、好奇等强烈的情绪或反应
senses.example: The minister remarks incited fierce anger among farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部长的讲话在农民中激起了强烈愤怒。
senses.why: The stirred action can be an emotion rather than a deed, so the common fire of the word image becomes anger, fear or curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 被催动的可以不只是一件事，也可以是一种情绪；核心画面里窜起的火苗，这时就成了愤怒、恐惧或好奇。

senses.title: Being incited, as in law
senses.definition: the legal act of encouraging another person to commit a crime, treated as an offence in itself
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指鼓动他人犯罪的行为，本身即构成可罚之罪
senses.example: He was charged with inciting racial hatred.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控煽动种族仇恨。
senses.why: Because the pushing is deliberate and public, courts name it as a crime of its own rather than as the later deed.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这种推动是有意而公开的，法律把它单独定为一宗罪，而不等后面的行为真的发生。

senses.title: To set a process or force in motion
senses.definition: to cause a change, a process or a physical reaction to start or to become more intense
senses.definitionCN: 使某种变化、进程或物理反应开始或变得更加剧烈
senses.example: Warm water might incite the seeds to sprout early.
senses.exampleCN: 温水可能会促使种子提早发芽。
senses.why: The earliest Latin sense was simply to move something quickly, without any moral judgement, and that bare sense of setting things going survives.
senses.whyCN: 最早的拉丁语义只是「使某物快速动起来」，不带道德评判；这种单纯的「让事情启动」，今天仍留在科学和日常的说法里。

intro.en: Incite comes from the Latin verb incitare, to set in rapid motion or urge on, built on citare, the frequentative of ciere, to move or summon.
intro.cn: incite 来自拉丁语动词 incitare，义为「使快速动起来、催促」，其词干 citare 是 ciere（使动、召唤）的反复形。

items.en: The form is a reconstructed root generally given as kei- meaning to set in motion; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语重构词根 kei-，意为「使动起来」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The verb ciere meant to move, set in motion or summon, and it produced citus, quick, and citare.
items.cn: 动词 ciere 意为「使动、使移动、召唤」，由此生出 citus「迅速的」与 citare。

items.en: The prefix in- added force, and incitare meant to drive forward, hasten or urge on, especially a horse or an army.
items.cn: 前缀 in- 加强语气，incitare 意为「驱策向前、催促」，尤用于驱马、催动军队。

items.en: English took the verb around the fifteenth century, first for urging forward and then for urging people into trouble.
items.cn: 英语大约在十五世纪引入这个动词，先表「催促向前」，再引申为催促别人去做出格的事。

items.en: The legal sense of inciting a crime or hatred took shape in the following centuries and remains the main modern use.
items.cn: 此后数百年间，「煽动犯罪或仇恨」的法律义逐渐定型，并成为今天最主要的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin cit- root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs that push people, from gentle encouragement to unlawful urging.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词根 cit- 构成的一族词；近义组收推动他人行动的动词，从温和鼓励到非法教唆。

entries.definition: Noun for the act of urging people to commit a crime or to act violently.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「煽动；挑唆」，法律上常指煽动行为本身，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A person who stirs others to do something reckless or unlawful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「煽动者；鼓动者」，指挑起他人行动的人。

entries.definition: A verb sharing citare but built on ex-; it means to stir interest or arousal, not to push anyone into wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，与本词共享 citare，但前缀为 ex-；义为「使兴奋、激发兴趣」，不带唆使他人犯法的色彩。

entries.definition: A verb from the same Latin stem meaning to quote or summon, with no prefix attached.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，来自同一拉丁词干，义为「引用；传唤」，不带前缀。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a single event or an unpleasant occurrence; it merely looks similar and comes from a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、事故」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To cause a strong reaction or an angry response; it can also mean to annoy deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激起、挑起（反应）」，也可指故意惹恼；比 incite 更侧重于引发反应本身。

entries.definition: To start a plot or trouble, especially secretly; it focuses on starting, while incite focuses on urging others.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、唆使（某事）」，常含暗中策划之意；侧重「起头」，而 incite 侧重「推动别人去做」。

entries.definition: To urge people publicly to act for a cause, or to stir up feelings; often used for political campaigns.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓动（公众）」，也指搅动情绪；常用于政治宣传，本身不一定含违法色彩。

entries.definition: To wake a feeling in someone, such as interest or suspicion; it is about the feeling, not about action.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「唤起、引起（情绪）」，如兴趣或怀疑；只谈情绪被唤起，不谈别人去行动。

entries.definition: To give support and confidence to someone; neutral or positive, and the neutral counterpart of incite.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓励、支持」，属中性或褒义，是与 incite 对照的中性说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root citare and the legal and news phrases where incite actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 citare，以及这个词实际出现的法律和新闻搭配。

normal.en: In plus citare, to set in motion: incite is the added push that gets people moving.
normal.cn: in 加 citare（使动）：incite 就是那多推的一把，把人推得动起来。

normal.en: The same citare family also gives excite and citation, all about moving or calling.
normal.cn: 同一 citare 词族还给出 excite 与 citation，都和「调动、召唤」有关。

normal.en: In court one is charged with inciting hatred or violence, not with the deed itself.
normal.cn: 在法庭上，人被控的是 inciting hatred、inciting violence，也就是煽动行为本身，而非后果。

normal.en: Incite sb to do sth is the standard frame: the target is the person, the object is the deed.
normal.cn: incite sb to do sth 是标准句型：被煽动的是人，被煽起来的是那件事。

normal.en: Compare excite: excite raises the temperature of feelings, incite pushes people over the line.
normal.cn: 对比 excite：excite 让情绪升温，incite 把人的行为推过界。

abstract.en: Picture a hand dropping one dry twig onto a pile of embers, and the flames leap up at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一根干柴丢进将熄的炭堆，火苗立刻蹿了起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a single shouted sentence that lights up a whole square of furious faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一句高喊的话，让整个广场上愤怒的面孔瞬间被点亮。

abstract.en: Think of a match struck in a courtroom: the striking itself is already the offence.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在法庭里划着一根火柴：划火这个动作本身就已经是罪了。

examples.en: The coach was accused of inciting his players to foul deliberately.
examples.cn: 这名教练被指煽动球员故意犯规。

examples.en: Wild rumours about the crash incited panic in the small town.
examples.cn: 关于坠机事故的流言在小镇激起了恐慌。

examples.en: Stirring up a crowd online can be punished as incitement to violence.
examples.cn: 在网上煽动人群可以被当作煽动暴力论处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引赛特」——把人引进赛场、催他往前冲，就是煽动；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ciere（使动、召唤）是其核心动词，反复形 citare 意为「催动、驱使」。前缀 in- 加强语气，构成 incitare「驱策向前、催促」，经英语化为 incite。同族有 excite、cite、citation。原始印欧语词根 kei-「使动起来」为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Incite always puts something into motion: first people into unlawful action, then feelings into heat, then the act itself in law, and finally any process or force that is set going.
sensesIntro.cn: incite 始终在「让什么动起来」：先把人推向违法行动，再把情绪烧热，然后是法律上把这个动作本身定罪，最后是任何进程或力量被启动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of dying embers and a hand adding one more dry twig.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆将熄的炭火，一只手又添进一根干柴。

branches.en: The deed line: the stirred person is urged toward something that breaks the law.
branches.cn: 行动线：被催动的人被推去做违法的事。

branches.en: The feeling line: the same stir happens inside people as anger or hatred.
branches.cn: 情绪线：同样的搅动发生在人心里，就变成愤怒或仇恨。

branches.en: The law line: courts punish the pushing itself, before the deed happens.
branches.cn: 法律线：法庭在行为发生之前就惩罚「推」这个动作本身。

branches.en: The process line: the word can move seeds, reactions or change without any person involved.
branches.cn: 进程线：这个词也可以推动种子、反应或变化，不涉及人。

branches.en: The fire image links them: urgent words and urgent anger are both flames leaping up.
branches.cn: 火的核心画面把两者连起来：急切的话和急切的怒火，都是蹿起来的火苗。

intro.en: Incite is a Latin verb of motion with a strengthening prefix; English adds its own noun and agent suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: incite 是一个带加强前缀的拉丁语动作动词，英语再以名词与施动者后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ciere, citare and incitare are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ciere、citare 与 incitare 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix adds force to the calm verb of motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给原本平缓的动作动词加上力度。

items.example: The verb is the moving root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的核心词根。

items.example: Citare gives English cite and excite.
items.exampleCN: citare 给出英语 cite 与 excite。

items.example: Incitare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: incitare 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.example: It forms incitement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 incitement。

items.example: It forms inciter.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inciter。

items.example: The same root with ex- gives excite.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根配上 ex- 就构成 excite。

items.example: The same root gives citation.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还给出 citation。

latinEntries.meaning: to urge on, set in rapid motion

definition_zh: （言语或想法）不连贯的；语无伦次的；不一致的；物理上不相干的
definition_en: not clear or logical, so that words, ideas or parts do not stick together into a whole
core_image: 一串珠子断了的线散在桌上，颗粒各自滚开，串不成一条
scene: 深夜的病房里，发烧的老人抓着护士的手，一句完整的话也说不出来。Burning with fever, the old man muttered an incoherent sentence and drifted back to sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 incoherent 是「（言语）不连贯、语无伦次的」（第 1 个义项：说话或行文失去连贯，难以理解）；句意：老人烧得厉害，咕哝了一句语无伦次的话又睡了过去。画面里有病床、输液瓶和握紧的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：不连贯的；语无伦次的；不一致的；（物理）不相干的

collocations.zh: 东拉西扯、没有条理的絮语

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ence 名词后缀构成，义为「不连贯；语无伦次；缺乏逻辑」
较旧的 -ency 名词形式，义同「不连贯」，现代多用 incoherence
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的肯定形式，义为「连贯的；有条理的；相干的」
肯定形式的派生名词，义为「连贯性；一致性」

senses.title: Speech or writing that does not stick together
senses.titleCN: 言语或文字不连贯、语无伦次
senses.definition: said or written in a way that is confused and disjointed, so listeners or readers cannot follow it
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行文混乱、跳跃，听者或读者无法顺畅理解
senses.example: Half asleep, she gave an incoherent answer to the nurse question.
senses.exampleCN: 半梦半醒间，她对医生的问题答得语无伦次。
senses.why: Hærēre means to stick, so coherent things stick together; with in- they do not, and one word fails to hold on to the next.
senses.whyCN: haerere 意为「黏住」，coherent 就是彼此黏连成一个整体；加上否定前缀 in- 后，词与词不再黏在一起，句子就散成了碎片。

senses.title: Ideas that do not fit into a system
senses.titleCN: （思路、论证、制度）缺乏条理、前后矛盾
senses.definition: describing ideas, arguments or policies that are confused, inconsistent or fail to form a logical whole
senses.definitionCN: 形容观点、论证或政策混乱不一，构不成一个合乎逻辑的整体
senses.example: The plan was ambitious but incoherent, and no two ministers agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划雄心勃勃却前后矛盾，两位部长之间也无法达成一致。
senses.why: The same absence of sticking is applied to parts of a system, where the pieces fail to join into a single design.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「黏不到一起」，只是对象从句子换成了一整套思路：各个部分拼不成一张完整的图纸。

senses.title: A mind or a movement that is disunited
senses.titleCN: （群体或运动）不一致、各行其是
senses.definition: describing a group, movement or person whose members hold different views and fail to act as one
senses.definitionCN: 形容群体、运动或个人意见分歧、无法凝聚成一体的状态
senses.example: Without a clear leader, the movement remained an incoherent collection of small groups.
senses.exampleCN: 没有明确领袖，这场运动始终只是一盘散沙般的小团体集合。
senses.why: Coherence can also mean joining together in purpose, so an incoherent group is one whose pieces keep rolling apart.
senses.whyCN: coherence 也指目标上的一致；incoherent 用在群体上，就是指这串珠子各自滚开，聚不成一条。

senses.title: Technical: waves that are not in step
senses.definition: describing light or sound waves whose phases are not in a fixed relationship, so they cannot interfere steadily
senses.definitionCN: 形容光波或声波的相位没有固定关系，因而不能稳定地产生干涉
senses.example: The lab used incoherent light from an ordinary lamp instead of a laser.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室用的是来自普通电灯的非相干光，而不是激光。
senses.why: The Latin image of parts that do not stick together matches waves whose crests do not line up, the technical branch of the same root.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「黏不到一起」的画面，在物理里就成了波峰对不齐：这正是同一词根在技术领域的分支。

intro.en: Incoherent is built in English, but its parts come from Latin: the prefix in-, the verb hærēre to stick, and the prefix co- meaning together.
intro.cn: incoherent 是在英语中组合而成的，但构件都来自拉丁语：否定前缀 in- 加 co-（一起）与 haerere（黏住）。

items.en: The verb is commonly traced to a root meaning to stick or cling, generally reconstructed as ghais-; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为可追溯到表示「黏附」的重构词根 ghais-；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Haerēre meant to stick, cling or be fixed, and gave such words as haerens and adhaerens, the source of adhere.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏附、贴住、固定」，由此生出 haerens、adhaerens（adhere 的来源）等词。

items.en: With co- meaning together, cohaerere meant to stick together, and its participle led to the English noun coherence, first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 加上表示「一起」的 co-，cohaerere 意为「黏在一起」，其分词经中古英语演化出名词 coherence，十六世纪见于英语。

items.en: Recorded Latin adjective incohaerens spelled out the negation directly; earlier English writers used the variant incoherent with a single h.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 incohaerens 直接写出否定；早期英语作家用过只写一个 h 的变体 incoherent。

items.en: The adjective incoherent is recorded from the seventeenth century, first for logically connected speech and later for groups and physical waves.
items.cn: 形容词 incoherent 在十七世纪有记录，最初指言语在逻辑上连不起来，后来扩展到群体与物理波动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin haerere root that sticks; the near-meaning group gathers words for confused content, each with a different kind of disorder.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 haerere「黏住」词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示混乱内容的词，各自的混乱方式并不相同。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning clear, logical and joined into a whole; the positive of incoherent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「连贯的、有条理的」；是 incoherent 的肯定形式。

entries.definition: Noun for the state of being confused, disconnected or lacking logic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不连贯、语无伦次、缺乏逻辑」，由本词加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Noun for the quality of being joined and consistent, the positive opposite of incoherence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连贯性、一致性」，是 incoherence 的肯定对应词。

entries.definition: Verb meaning to stick to a surface or to follow a rule closely; built from the same Latin stick verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「黏附；坚持、遵守」，由同一拉丁「黏附」动词构成。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning existing as a natural part of something; same root, but the in- here means inward, not not.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「固有的、内在的」；同根，但这里的 in- 表示「里面」，不是否定。

entries.definition: Adjective for something unclear or muddled; about the muddy state itself rather than the failure to join.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「混乱的、不清楚的」；强调状态本身浑浊，而不强调各部分连不起来。

entries.definition: Adjective for parts that do not connect smoothly; very close to incoherent when used of talk or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「脱节的、不连贯的」，用于讲话或文章时与 incoherent 很近。

entries.definition: Adjective for long talk that wanders off the subject; longer and looser than simply incoherent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漫无边际的、东拉西扯的」，比 incoherent 更强调冗长且跑题。

entries.definition: Adjective for a message that has been distorted until it is hard to understand, such as a bad phone signal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「（信息）被弄乱、含混不清的」，常指信号或转述导致的内容失真。

entries.definition: Adjective for reasoning that breaks the rules of logic; the parts may stick together but the chain of proof is broken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合逻辑的」；部件或许连着，但推理链断了。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin stick root haerere plus the prefix pattern that builds the positive and negative pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「黏住」词根 haerere，以及构成肯定与否定词对的相同前缀结构。

normal.en: Change the prefix to remember the pair: coherent sticks together, incoherent does not.
normal.cn: 换一个前缀就能成对记忆：coherent 黏在一起，incoherent 黏不起来。

normal.en: The stick root haerere also gives adhere and adhesion, where things truly cling.
normal.cn: 「黏住」词根 haerere 还给出 adhere、adhesion，那里是真的在黏。

normal.en: Incoherent speech is the phrase of the sickroom and the courtroom alike.
normal.cn: incoherent speech 既出现在病房，也出现在法庭记录里。

normal.en: The noun pair incoherence and coherence names the quality that is missing or present.
normal.cn: 名词对 incoherence 与 coherence 正好标出「缺」与「有」的那种连贯性。

normal.en: Compare inherent, which shares the root but uses in- to mean inside, not no.
normal.cn: 对比 inherent：同根，但那里的 in- 表示「里面」，而不是否定。

abstract.en: Picture a string of beads whose thread has snapped, and each bead rolls off in its own direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一串断了线的珠子，每颗都往自己的方向滚去。

abstract.en: Listen to a radio losing its station: words crack and break apart so no sentence holds.
abstract.cn: 想象一台收音机跑台，词语碎裂断开，没有一句话站得住。

abstract.en: See a crowd all pulling in different directions, never forming one shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人各自往不同方向拉，永远拼不成一个整体。

examples.en: He was too tired to explain clearly and his account came out incoherent.
examples.cn: 他太累了，讲不清楚，叙述显得不连贯。

examples.en: The essay is lively but full of incoherent jumps from one topic to another.
examples.cn: 这篇文章生动，却充满毫无条理的跳跃，从一个话题跳到另一个。

examples.en: A witness described the accident in an incoherent rush of words.
examples.cn: 一名目击者语无伦次地匆忙描述了事故经过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬扣·黑伦」——硬把珠子扣在一起，结果还是散落一桌，就是「不连贯」；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 haerere「黏住、贴附」是核心词根，加 co-（一起）后 cohaerere 意为「黏在一起」，其肯定形 coherent 指「连贯的」。前缀 in- 表示否定，构成 incohaerens，英语化为 incoherent，即各部分黏不起来。同根词有 adhere、adhesion、inherent。原始印欧语词根 ghais-「黏附」为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of incoherent is one failed sticking: words that will not join into a sentence, ideas that will not join into a plan, people who will not join into one movement, and waves that will not join in phase.
sensesIntro.cn: incoherent 的每个义项都是一种「黏不起来」：词黏不成句，想法黏不成计划，人黏不成一股力量，波黏不成同一相位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snapped thread and loose beads scattered across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：断了线的珠子和散落一桌的颗粒。

branches.en: The language line: one word will not hold on to the next, so the sentence falls apart.
branches.cn: 语言线：前一个词抓不住后一个词，句子就散架了。

branches.en: The logic line: parts of an argument or plan fail to fit into one design.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：论证或计划的各部分拼不成一张图纸。

branches.en: The community line: members go their own ways instead of holding together.
branches.cn: 群体线：成员各走各的，无法抱成一团。

branches.en: The physics line: waves fail to keep a fixed phase, the technical form of not sticking.
branches.cn: 物理线：波的相位对不齐，是「黏不住」的技术形态。

branches.en: The three share one remedy: something must be added that lets loose parts hold together again.
branches.cn: 这三条共享同一个补救方向：得有人补上一点什么，让散开的部件重新黏合。

intro.en: Incoherent is a negative adjective built from a Latin stick verb; English adds its own noun and adverb suffixes around the same root.
intro.cn: incoherent 是由拉丁语「黏住」动词构成的否定形容词，英语再以名词与副词后缀围绕同一词根扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere, cohaerere and incohaerens are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haerere、cohaerere 与 incohaerens 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix turns coherent into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把 coherent 变成它的反义。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of things sticking together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「黏在一起」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the sticking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的核心词根。

items.structure: Latin verb from co- plus haerere
items.example: The verb yields English coherence.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出英语 coherence。

items.example: The Late Latin adjective is the direct model for the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁形容词是英语词形的直接范本。

items.example: It forms coherent and its negative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 coherent 及其否定形式。

items.example: It forms incoherence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 incoherence。

items.example: It forms incoherently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 incoherently。

items.example: The same root gives adhesion.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还给出 adhesion。

definition_zh: （邮件、电话、消息）收到的；进来的；（人员）新来的、上任的；（选举中）即将获胜的
definition_en: coming in from outside toward a place or a person, often used of messages, calls, visitors, staff or election results
core_image: 一个箭头穿过门框，由外向内直指屋子中央
scene: 清晨的办公室还空着，桌上那部电话忽然震了一下，屏幕亮起来。She picked up the handset and took the incoming call before the second ring.
sceneCN: 这里 incoming 是「（电话）打进来的」（第 1 个义项：信号或消息从外界进入）；句意：她拿起听筒，在电话响第二声之前就接起了打进来的电话。画面里有震动的电话、亮起的屏幕和空着的办公桌。

pos.zh: 形容词：进来的；收到的；（人员）新来的；（选举）即将获胜的
名词：进入的东西；收入（incomings 复数形式）

collocations.zh: 即将就任的主席（或总统）

derivatives.zh: 由 incoming 加 call 构成的复合名词，义为「来电」
由 on 加 coming 构成的近邻复合词，义为「迎面而来的」，如迎面车辆与来潮
由 up 加 coming 构成的复合词，义为「即将到来的、即将发生的」
取反方向前缀 out- 构成的反义复合词，义为「外向的；即将离任的」

senses.title: Messages and signals arriving from outside
senses.titleCN: （来电、邮件、消息）收到的、进来的
senses.definition: describing calls, letters, messages or signals that are arriving at a person or place from somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 形容电话、信件、消息或信号从外部到达某人或某地
senses.example: The assistant screened every incoming email for the director.
senses.exampleCN: 助理替主任筛选所有收到的邮件。
senses.why: Come in means to arrive inside, and the old participle coming plus in- simply names what is on its way in.
senses.whyCN: come in 意为「进来」；古英语的 coming 加上表示「进入」的 in-，说的就是「正往里面来」的东西。

senses.title: People or vehicles arriving at a place
senses.titleCN: （乘客、航班、旅客）到达的、进港的
senses.definition: describing troops, flights, passengers or traffic that are approaching or arriving at a place
senses.definitionCN: 形容部队、航班、旅客或车流正接近或抵达某地
senses.example: The airport closed one runway while an incoming flight had to wait.
senses.exampleCN: 机场关闭了一条跑道，一架进港航班只好等待。
senses.why: The arrow that points into a building also points into a city, an airport or a harbour, so arrivals of people and vehicles take the same word.
senses.whyCN: 指向屋内的箭头同样可以指向城市、机场或港口，于是人和交通工具的「到达」也沿用同一词形。

senses.title: A person taking up a new post
senses.definition: describing someone who is about to begin a job or take over an office and is moving into the role
senses.definitionCN: 形容即将开始任职或接任某个职位、正进入该角色的人
senses.example: The incoming manager spent a week sitting with the outgoing team.
senses.exampleCN: 新上任的经理花了一周时间和即将离任的团队待在一起。
senses.why: A person moves into a post the way a signal moves into a room, so the incoming manager is one coming in to take the chair.
senses.whyCN: 人进入职位，就像信号进入房间：incoming 形容的正是那位「进来接椅子」的新任者。

senses.title: Election results that are becoming certain
senses.definition: used of members or officials who are winning an election, or of results that are coming in as votes are counted
senses.definitionCN: 指在选举中正在胜出的当选人，或计票过程中陆续传来的结果
senses.example: The incoming senator promised to visit every district in his first year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位即将上任的参议员承诺第一年内走访每个选区。
senses.why: Votes come in and a winner comes in, so the arrivals at a counting desk keep the same arrow-into-the-room image.
senses.whyCN: 票陆续「进来」，胜出者也是「进来」的：计票桌前到达的东西，沿用同一个「箭头进屋」的画面。

senses.title: The noun: what comes in, or money received
senses.definition: a noun for things that come in, especially money or goods received, more often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指进入的东西，尤指收到的钱财或货物，多用复数形式
senses.example: The charity keeps track of its incomings and outgoings each month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构每月记录其收入与支出。
senses.why: By conversion the adjective becomes a plain noun, and whatever arrives can be counted as an incoming or an incomings total.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接转成名词，凡是「进来了的东西」都可以清点成一项 incoming，复数就成了一本收支账。

intro.en: Incoming is an English compound of the old Germanic adverb in and the participle coming, first used for income and then for whatever is arriving.
intro.cn: incoming 是英语由古日耳曼语副词 in 加分词 coming 构成的复合词，先用于「收入」，后扩展到一切「正在到来的」东西。

items.en: The adverb in descends from the Proto-Germanic *in, which already marked position inside.
items.cn: 副词 in 源自原始日耳曼语 *in，当时就已表示「在……里面」。

items.en: Old English used the adverb inn for into and the verb cuman for to come, together spelling out the motion of arriving inside.
items.cn: 古英语用副词 inn 表示「进入」，用动词 cuman 表示「来」，合起来就是「进入」这个动作。

items.en: The participle coming was joined with the adverb in to name what is on its way in.
items.cn: 分词 coming 与副词 in 结合，用来指称「正往里面来」的东西。

items.en: Early records use incomings for money and rent received, the ancestor of the modern accounting sense.
items.cn: 早期记录用 incomings 表示收到的钱财与租金，是现代会计用法「收入」的前身。

items.en: Telegraph and telephone gave incoming call and incoming mail, and elections added the incoming member.
items.cn: 电报与电话带来了 incoming call、incoming mail，选举又带来了 incoming member 这样的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other composites of the same coming and in- pieces; the near-meaning group gathers words for arriving or upcoming, each with a different direction or timing.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由 coming 或 in- 构件组成的其他复合词；近义组收表示到达或未来的词，方向与时间各不相同。

entries.definition: Adjective for things leaving a place, or for a person who is friendly and open; the direction opposite of incoming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「外发的；外向的；即将离任的」，是本词的方向反义。

entries.definition: Adjective for something moving toward you, such as oncoming traffic; the prefix here is on, not in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迎面而来的」，如迎面车流；前缀是 on 而不是 in，与本词容易混淆但方向不同。

entries.definition: Adjective for something that will happen soon in the future, from up plus coming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「即将到来的、即将发生的」，由 up 加 coming 构成。

entries.definition: Noun for a mass arrival of people or things; it merely looks similar with in- and comes from Latin fluere, to flow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「涌入」，指人或物大量进入；只是都带 in- 而看上去相近，词源是拉丁语 fluere「流动」，与本词不同。

entries.definition: Noun meaning the act of entering; it also starts with in- but comes from Latin gradi, to step.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」；同样以 in- 开头，但词源是拉丁语 gradi「迈步」，与本词构词不同。
