entries.definition: The participle of arrive, used for a traveller or a train that has reached the end of a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 arrive 的分词，指已经到达终点的旅客或列车；强调「抵达」，而非「进入」。

entries.definition: Adjective for something coming from another country or outside the group; it marks origin, not direction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「外国的、外来的」；强调来源在外，而不是运动方向向内。

entries.definition: Adjective for traffic or shipments travelling toward a centre; close to incoming in logistics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「入境的、运入的」，常用于交通与物流，和 incoming 在货运语境里很接近。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning happening a short time ago; it shares the idea of news that has just arrived.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最近的、刚发生的」，与「刚到的消息」这一理念相近。

entries.definition: Noun or adjective for a time still to come; upcoming looks forward, while incoming looks at what is coming toward now.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，指「未来」；upcoming 面向将来，而 incoming 指正朝现在而来的东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain built-in meaning of in plus coming, and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用 in 加 coming 本身就有的字面意思，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Read it literally: in plus coming, something that is coming in.
normal.cn: 按字面读：in 加 coming，就是「正在进来的东西」。

normal.en: Swap in for out and you get outgoing, which sets the opposite direction.
normal.cn: 把 in 换成 out 就得到 outgoing，方向正好相反。

normal.en: Incoming call, incoming mail and incoming flight all share the arrow pointing into a place.
normal.cn: incoming call、incoming mail、incoming flight 共用一个指向某地的箭头。

normal.en: Incoming and outgoing staff are the two sides of a handover.
normal.cn: incoming 与 outgoing 的人员，正是一次交接的两端。

normal.en: Incomings in plural often means money received on an account.
normal.cn: 复数 incomings 常指账上收到的钱，即收入。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow crossing a doorway and stopping right in the middle of the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个箭头穿过门框，停在屋子正中。

abstract.en: Hear a phone buzz once and see the screen light up before the second ring.
abstract.cn: 想象电话震了一下，屏幕亮起，还没等第二声铃响。

abstract.en: See a new manager walking in and an older one walking out through the same door.
abstract.cn: 想象一位新经理进门、一位老经理出门，走过同一扇门。

examples.en: Please hold all incoming calls until the meeting ends.
examples.cn: 会议结束之前，请把所有来电都挂起。

examples.en: The incoming train was late because of heavy snow.
examples.cn: 由于大雪，这趟进站列车晚点了。

examples.en: The incoming head of department plans a full review.
examples.cn: 即将上任的系主任计划做一次全面复查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「音·康明」——门外有人喊一声「快来」，就是有东西正往门里进，所以 incoming 是「进来的」；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由日耳曼语系固有的副词 in（进入）与分词 coming（来、到来）复合而成，字面就是「正往里面来」。同族复合词有 outgoing（反方向）、oncoming（迎面）、upcoming（即将到来）。

sensesIntro.en: Incoming always points an arrow into a place: first messages into a home or office, then vehicles and people into a city, then a new officer into a post, a winner into an office, and at last the money that has come in.
sensesIntro.cn: incoming 始终把箭头指向一个目的地：先是消息进入家或办公室，再是车辆与人进入城市，然后是新人进入职位、当选者进入官署，最后是已经进来的钱财。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow crossing a doorway and stopping at the centre of the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个箭头穿过门框，停在屋子正中。

branches.en: The traffic line: messages, calls and flights are all arrows heading toward a doorstep.
branches.cn: 流动线：消息、电话与航班都是飞向门口的那个箭头。

branches.en: The office line: a new officer and a new winner come in through the same door as the mail.
branches.cn: 职位线：新任官员与当选者，和信件一样从这扇门进来。

branches.en: The money line: what has come in can be counted, and the noun keeps the total.
branches.cn: 钱财线：已经进来的东西可以清点，名词形式保留了这个总数。

branches.en: The signal line is the most common modern use, from phones and email to radio and radar.
branches.cn: 信号线是现代最常见的用法，从电话、邮件到无线电与雷达都用它。

branches.en: The two extremes: a person coming into an office, and an office counting what came into it.
branches.cn: 两端对照：一个即将进门就任的人，与一个正在清点进账的部门。

intro.en: Incoming is not a Latin derivation but a Germanic-style compound: the native prefix in plus the English participle coming, with the same pieces also yielding outgoing and oncoming.
intro.cn: incoming 并不是拉丁语派生词，而是日耳曼式的复合词：本族副词 in 加英语分词 coming；同类构件还构成 outgoing、oncoming 等词。

latinIntro.en: The elements here are native English, so there is no Latin family of the same prefix and root; the nearest Latin relatives come from other roots altogether.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的构件都是英语本族成分，并没有同前缀同词根的拉丁词族；最接近的拉丁词其实来自完全不同的词根。

items.example: The adverb supplies the inward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词提供向内的方向。

items.example: The verb gives the base of the participle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供分词词干。

items.example: It forms coming from come.
items.exampleCN: 它把 come 变成 coming。

items.example: The compound keeps the plain meaning of its parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了各构件最字面的意思。

items.example: The opposite prefix gives outgoing.
items.exampleCN: 取反的前缀给出 outgoing。

items.example: With on- we get oncoming.
items.exampleCN: 换上 on- 就得到 oncoming。

items.example: With up- we get upcoming.
items.exampleCN: 换上 up- 就得到 upcoming。

items.example: The plural incomings names money received.
items.exampleCN: 复数 incomings 指收到的钱款。

definition_zh: 无与伦比的；不能相比的；不可比的
definition_en: so good that nothing else can be compared with it, or unable to be compared because the things differ in kind
core_image: 一架天平：一端放着某个人或某件事，另一端找不到能与之配平的砝码
scene: 她看完那场独舞后久久不说话。After the solo dance, the judges said her stage presence was incomparable.
sceneCN: 这里 incomparable 是「无与伦比的」（第 1 个义项：好到没有东西能与之相比）；句意：独舞结束后，评委说她的台风无与伦比。

pos.zh: 无与伦比的；不能相比的；不可比的

derivatives.zh: 由 incomparable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「无可比拟；不可比性」
同族基础动词，义为「比较；对比」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的形式，义为「可比的；类似的」
由 compare 加名词后缀 -ison 构成，义为「比较；对照」

senses.title: So good that no peer exists
senses.definition: so excellent that nothing else can be compared with it
senses.definitionCN: 出色到没有其他事物可以与之相比
senses.example: The valley is famous for its incomparable scenery.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷以其无与伦比的景色闻名。
senses.why: In- says not, and the base verb compare says to set side by side, so incomparable first means nothing can stand beside it.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 表示「不」，基础动词 compare 表示「并排放着比较」，所以这个词首先指没有任何东西能与之并排。

senses.title: Too different to be compared
senses.definition: too different in kind from something else for a fair comparison to be made
senses.definitionCN: 在种类上差别太大，无法进行公平的比较
senses.example: A novel and a painting are incomparable as works of art.
senses.exampleCN: 作为艺术作品，小说和绘画是不可比的。
senses.why: When two things belong to different kinds, the scales have no matching weight, and the comparison itself collapses.
senses.whyCN: 当两样东西属于不同的类别时，天平上找不到匹配的砝码，比较这件事本身就不成立。

senses.title: Missing an equal
senses.definition: having no equal among people, especially in skill or status
senses.definitionCN: 在人当中没有对手，尤指在技艺或地位上
senses.example: As a teacher she was incomparable in patience.
senses.exampleCN: 作为老师，她在耐心上无人能及。
senses.why: The superlative sense narrows from things to people, describing someone whose peers cannot be found on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个最高级含义从事物缩小到人，描述某人在天平上找不到同级对手。

senses.title: Literary hyperbole
senses.definition: used in literature and praise to describe beauty or greatness that ordinary words cannot measure
senses.definitionCN: 在文学与赞美中用来形容寻常词语无法衡量的美或伟大
senses.example: Poets called her smile incomparable, beyond all earthly praise.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人们称她的微笑无与伦比，世间任何赞美都不足以形容。
senses.why: The same absence of a peer becomes an expressive device, refusing to name anything equal rather than naming what is great.
senses.whyCN: 同样是找不到同级者，这里变成一种表达手段：不指出美好之处，而是拒绝给出任何相当之物。

intro.en: Incomparable joins Latin in-, not, to comparabilis, from comparare, to compare, itself from compar, a peer.
intro.cn: incomparable 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加 comparabilis 构成，后者来自 comparare（比较），而 comparare 又出自 compar（同级者）。

items.en: Par means equal, and the prefixed compar names a peer, a person of the same rank.
items.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为「相等」，加前缀后的 compar 指「同级之人、地位相当者」。

items.en: Comparare builds on compar and means to pair things up or compare them.
items.cn: comparare 由 compar 构成，意为「配对、加以比较」。

items.en: The adjective comparabilis, able to be compared, is formed with the suffix -bilis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语用后缀 -bilis 构成形容词 comparabilis，意为「可以比较的」。

items.en: French incomparable carries the negated form with the prefix in-, and it passes into English about the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 incomparable 带着否定前缀 in- 传入英语，约在十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: English keeps the negated sense, often in high praise, as in incomparable beauty.
items.cn: 英语保留了否定含义，多用于高度赞美，如「绝美」。

note.en: Incomparable sits at the negative end of the compare family, beside its own base compare, and near praise words that also deny any rival.
note.cn: incomparable 处在比较这一词族的否定一端，与它的基础词 compare 相邻，也和那些同样否认对手的赞美词相邻。

entries.definition: to examine two things to see how they differ
similar enough to be compared
in a way that has no equal
better than everyone else at something
so good that nothing can equal it
having no equal among one peers

normalIntro.en: Incomparable is built from compare: in- turns the act of comparing off, because no second thing exists to set beside the first.
normalIntro.cn: incomparable 由 compare 构成：前缀 in- 把比较这个动作关掉，因为根本找不到第二样东西可以放在第一样旁边。

normal.en: In- is the Latin prefix for not, so incomparable is literally not comparable.
normal.cn: in- 是拉丁语表示「不」的前缀，所以 incomparable 字面就是「不可比较」。

normal.en: The base verb compare comes from Latin compar, a peer of the same rank.
normal.cn: 基础动词 compare 来自拉丁语 compar，指地位相当的「同级者」。

normal.en: Incomparable beauty is a fixed praise for scenery, music, or a person.
normal.cn: incomparable beauty 是形容风景、音乐或人的固定赞美语。

normal.en: Incomparable to and incomparable with both mean beyond comparison.
normal.cn: incomparable to 与 incomparable with 都表示「无法相比」。

normal.en: Compare comparable: comparable means fit to be compared, incomparable means no fit partner can be found.
normal.cn: 对比 comparable：comparable 表示「可以比较」，incomparable 表示「找不到合适的比较对象」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with one pan full and the other pan empty forever.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端装满，另一端永远空着。

abstract.en: Imagine two objects of different kinds placed on the same measuring table.
abstract.cn: 想象两件种类完全不同的东西被放到同一张测量台上。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd where every face is turned away from the champion.
abstract.cn: 想象人群里每一张脸都背对着冠军。

examples.en: The orchestra gave an incomparable performance of the symphony.
examples.cn: 乐团把这首交响曲演绎得无与伦比。

examples.en: For a young singer, her confidence was incomparable.
examples.cn: 对一位年轻歌手来说，她的自信无人能比。

examples.en: Because the two languages differ so much, their idioms are often incomparable.
examples.cn: 由于两种语言差别太大，它们的习语常常无法相互比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + come + par + able」——什么也「来」不了，没法并排配成一对，就是无与伦比。这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ comparare（比较，源自 compar「同级者」）→ 晚期拉丁语 comparabilis（可比的）→ 古法语 incomparable → 英语 incomparable，核心义「找不到同级者」。

sensesIntro.en: Incomparable starts from the picture of a scale with no matching weight, then spreads to things of different kinds that defy comparison, to people without an equal, and finally to literary praise.
sensesIntro.cn: incomparable 从「天平上找不到匹配砝码」的画面出发，先指好到无人可比，再指类别不同而无法比较，接着指人无对手，最后成为文学赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale with one side loaded and no weight that can balance it.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端压着重物，另一端找不到能配平的砝码。

branches.en: Supreme quality is the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 最高品质是日常最主要的义项。

branches.en: Things of different kinds cannot be placed on the same scale.
branches.cn: 类别不同的事物无法放到同一架天平上。

branches.en: The personal sense names someone without peers.
branches.cn: 指人的义项表示没有同级对手。

branches.en: Literary praise refuses to name any equal at all.
branches.cn: 文学赞美干脆拒绝给出任何相当之物。

branches.en: Excellence in an art or a skill is often praised as incomparable in a person.
branches.cn: 某人在艺术或技艺上的卓越，常被人以「无与伦比」来赞美。

intro.en: Incomparable is a negative English adjective built on the Latin root par, equal, through the verb family compare, comparable, comparison.
intro.cn: incomparable 是在拉丁词根 par（相等）之上、经由 compare、comparable、comparison 这一动词族构成的否定形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin par means equal, compar means a peer, and comparare means to compare; in- negates the whole.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，compar 意为同级者，comparare 意为比较；前缀 in- 否定整个词。

items.example: Par is the tiny root under a long word family.
items.exampleCN: par 是这个长词族底下的小词根。

items.example: A compar is someone you can stand beside as an equal.
items.exampleCN: compar 指可以与你平等并立的人。

items.example: Comparare gives English compare.
items.exampleCN: comparare 演变成英语的 compare。

items.example: The suffix -bilis turns comparare into comparabilis.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -bilis 把 comparare 变成 comparabilis。

items.example: Comparabilis is the direct ancestor of comparable.
items.exampleCN: comparabilis 是 comparable 的直接祖先。

items.example: The prefix in- negates comparabilis.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 否定 comparabilis。

items.example: Comparable is the positive partner of incomparable.
items.exampleCN: comparable 是 incomparable 的肯定搭档。

items.example: Incomparable means that no peer can be found.
items.exampleCN: incomparable 表示找不到同级者。

items.example: The suffix -able forms comparable from compare.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 使 compare 变成 comparable。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms incomparably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 incomparably。
